articleTitle: Machine Learning to Enhance the V2V Communication-based IoD Using Companding Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper investigates the improvement of Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communications in the Internet of Drones (IoD) scenario for the reduction of the Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) problem in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) systems. Motivated by the recent research on machine learning and deep neural network, this study will attempt to optimize Quality of Service (QoS) by means of a multiprocessing approach based on Daubechies wavelets. The proposed scheme integrates high-performance PAPR reduction schemes, such as µ-law companding, hybrid precoding-companding, and neural network-based adaptive algorithms. Deep reinforcement learning-driven approach in clipping and filtering is further proposed, which can offer real-time adaptation for the high-demanding communications. Results show a considerable gain in PAPR, over 60% PAPR reduction under high SNR conditions. These findings show that IoD can sustain stable V2V connections in urban use cases, thereby providing a scalable solution for 5G and beyond networks.

articleTitle: APO-Optimized ARX-Based System Identification of a Ship Maneuvering System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The identification of dynamic models for ships is essential in marine and maritime engineering, as it facilitates accurate prediction and control of vessel behavior. Traditional ship system identification methods involve identifying a few parameters from the dynamic model. Only simplified linearized models have utilized metaheuristic techniques for ship identification recently. This paper describes a new way to use the Artificial Protozoa Optimization (APO) algorithm to make an Autoregression with Exogenous Input (ARX) model for the full ship dynamics work better. The adaptive foraging, dormancy, and reproduction behaviors of protozoa gave rise to the APO algorithm, which is a strong metaheuristic framework for parameter optimization. By leveraging the APO, we aim to enhance the accuracy of ship dynamics identification and its explainability. Evaluation of the model on the provided test data demonstrates that the APO-optimized ARX model provides excellent identification compared to results from existing methods, achieving a mean R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.9437, thus providing a reliable and efficient tool for ship maneuvering identification.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Based on the Parity Space Approach for Neutral Time Delay Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A Fault Detection and Isolation (FDI) scheme for discrete neutral time-delay systems is introduced, designed for effective fault detection and isolation. This approach addresses the unique characteristics of neutral delays by employing a time-delay operator, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex>, which captures the effects of both the delayed state and its derivative. Residuals are derived by recursively applying the system equations within a parity space framework, providing a robust basis for fault detection. Additionally, a generalized residual set is developed by leveraging the redundancy in the parity space, allowing for comprehensive fault detection and isolation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through a numerical example.

articleTitle: Temperature Effects on Electrical Characteristics of 20 nm Finfet Transistor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this work, the effects of electrical polarization on 20 nm FinFET devices are studied at various temperature values. FinFET operation is described using an electrical model based on an enhanced drift-diffusion (D-D) model. However, we introduce a new expression for electron mobility to improve the D-D model. The Finite Element Method is employed to obtain results. Based on experimental and numerical results, our model can effectively interpret the degradation of electrical characteristics in the studied FinFET. Moreover, this research demonstrates that the temperature significantly impacts the IDS-VDS characteristics of the studied FinFET, leading to a decrease in performance.

articleTitle: Fully Transparent and Self-Powered Planar Photodetector Based on $\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$ Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this study, both simulation and elaboration of a planar fully transparent photodetector based on beta gallium oxide (β-Ga203) semiconductor as absorption layer has been carried out. The device in question is simulated and elaborated based on low cost technological process and relatively high electrical and optical performances. The latter consist of quartz as a substrate, Ga203 thin film at beta phase with n-type semiconductor layer. Both indium zinc tin oxide (IZTO) and indium tin oxide (ITO) were used as Schottky and ohmic contacts, respectively. This selection of materials was made according to their low cost and availability, their high electrical and optical properties. The dark versus illumination current result shows an important contrast ratio. 0.18 AIW and 98 % prove the high performance of the elaborated photodetector for the responsivity and the quantum efficiency, respectively.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Estimation of States and Sensor Faults Based on a Multiobserver Structure for Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The present paper proposes a multi-observer structure for nonlinear systems in the presence of sensor faults. These faults are considered as auxiliary state variables; thus, a descriptor system is constructed based on a decoupled multimodel. Thanks to this descriptor structure, the proposed multiobserver provides more degrees of freedom in the design procedure and simultaneous robust estimation of the states and the sensor faults without any assumption concerning the fault dynamics. The Lyapunov approach is exploited to establish the stability conditions that are expressed via Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). The superiority of the proposed strategy is illustrated through simulation results and a comparative study.

articleTitle: Saving Study for Consumed in the Lighting System of a Milk Factory in Tripoli Operated on PV
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: To address the problem of illumination intensity resulting from the different usable ages, this study calculated the cost of replacing fluorescent lamps in a dairy factory located in Tripoli, Libya, which operates on a photovoltaic system before and after the end of its useful life. The aim of the study was to save electricity to reduce the load on the solar energy system, as the number of lamps was 6000 lamps. This also helped address the problem of the high cost of replacing damaged lamps individually. Using mathematical formulas as a technique, it was determined that replacing lamps at the end of their useful life costs 42,000 Libyan dinars annually, while replacing lamps after their useful life costs 84,000 Libyan dinars during the same period of time. This means that there are annual savings of 48.21% or 43,500 Libyan dinars. While preserving the transformers and wires, in addition to selling the replaced lamps that can be used again.

articleTitle: Design and Conception of an IoT-Controlled UV-C Sterilization System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Due to the emergence of infectious diseases through the air in recent years, the disinfection of high-risk contamination spaces, such as hospitals and large surfaces, has become an essential task in order to ensure better health safety against bacteria and viruses. Ultraviolet (UV) light has been widely recognized for its effectiveness in eliminating pathogenic microorganisms. It has proven to be effective in various applications, including healthcare facilities, laboratories, food processing industries, and public spaces. This project focuses on the use of the UV light for the area's sterilization operation, and proposes the development of a smartphone-controlled disinfection system: from the prototype to a commercial product dedicated to spaces with high aseptic requirements. Our conception is based on a passive infrared motion sensor (PIR) HC-SR501, an ESP32 microcontroller, a TFT touch screen and a mobile application connected with a server cloud and an UV-C lamp emitting shortwavelength ultraviolet light of 254 nm. The proposed prototype has been tested in a biological laboratory, at a distance of 250 cm and over an exposure time of 20 minutes, no bacterial colonies were detected, These biological test results approves the lamp's effectiveness and confirms the use validity of this technology for disinfection in healthcare-sensitive environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Breast Ultrasound Diagnostics Using GANs and Guided Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In ultrasound imaging, speckle noise presents a significant challenge, undermining image clarity and the accuracy of diagnostic interpretations. To address this critical issue, We develop a new method for improving the quality of ultrasound images using a Denoising Generative Adversarial Network complemented by a Guided Filter (DNGAN-GF). This method uses a neural network architecture to learn how to generate denoised images from noisy inputs while preserving important anatomical contours and details. Our innovative approach effectively transforms noisy images into remarkably clear visual representations. The DNGAN learns to capture the characteristics of clean image data, while the GF refines the results, ensuring the fidelity of anatomical structures. Qualitative assessments conducted by experts highlight the exceptional sharpness of contours and anatomical features, making anomaly interpretation more intuitive and accessible. This improvement not only assists radiologists in their evaluations but also has the potential to reduce diagnostic errors. Quantitative analyses reveal substantial increases in PSNR and SSIM metrics, confirming the superiority of our proposed DNGAN-GF method compared to conventional techniques. By significantly enhancing the visibility of anatomical details, our proposed solution can improve diagnostic accuracy and redefine standards in medical imaging, ultimately elevating the quality of patient care.

articleTitle: Exploiting Persistent Vibration Phenomena and MEMS Conversion Effects at the Castello Ursino Museum (Sicily, Italy)
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper explores persistent vibration phenomena measured at the Castello Ursino Museum in Catania and their effects, analyzed through Aluminum Nitride (AlN) Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) transducers. The study aims to utilize the Tromino® measurement system to assess the structural dynamics and vibration behavior of the museum. By analyzing vibration data, the research identifies areas with persistent vibrations that can serve as optimal sites for placing MEMS sensors, thereby maximizing energy harvesting for autonomous monitoring. Through damping analysis, the study highlights regions within the museum, particularly the primary Pinacoteca Room on the second level, where vibrations are most significant. These vibrations are attributed to factors such as structural dynamics, visitor movement, and nearby traffic. While these areas offer potential for increased energy capture, it is also essential to monitor high levels of vibration, as they can be potentially critical for the conservation of artifacts. Measurement campaigns conducted both in the laboratory and on-site demonstrate the feasibility of this approach for applications in cultural heritage sites and environments of historical and artistic interest. This research contributes to the development of energy-efficient, autonomous solutions, advancing the preservation and monitoring of culturally significant and architecturally complex sites such as the Castello Ursino Museum.

articleTitle: Improving Data Acquisition For a Quartz Crystal Microbalance Electrochemical Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This article explores the development of a scalable, contemporary interface designed to replace outdated laboratory control systems. Utilizing Python open source codes like PyVISA, PyQt, and the Prologix GPIB-USB controller, this solution automates the measurement of essential parameters, including frequency and voltage. It meets the requirements of contemporary electrochemical studies with its real-time data acquisition, enhance precision and user-friendly interface. The new developed interface is a flexible to promote scientific investigation since it guarantees dependently, flexibility and enhanced performance.

articleTitle: On Functional Interval Observer Design for Fault Estimation of Discrete-Time Linear Parameter Varying Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: An interval fault estimation methodology for Linear Parameter Variable (LPV) systems with uncertainties and actuator faults is presented in this paper. Firstly, an augmented system is defined using state augmentation method. Secondly, an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\infty}$</tex> technique is introduced to minimise the effects of uncertainties and to enhance the estimation precision. The observer design conditions are expressed in terms of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). Then, the envelopes of the fault can be determined using the obtained state estimation. Finally, a simulation studies is presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Deep learning YOLOv5s Model for Tiny Pests Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The whiteflies are one of the most destructive tiny insects found in high-yielding crops, and because of their wide range of spread, they can seriously harm agriculture. Because these pest species cause insufficient agricultural production on a large scale, it is challenging and time-consuming for humans to observe these insects in a larger field. Recently, deep learning has been applied to agriculture to detect plant pests. This study proposes using the YOLOv5s convolutional neural network algorithm to identify whiteflies on plant leaves and add this data to the whitefly dataset repository. A comparative analysis was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the model when subjected to the pre-processing technique of tilling, as well as data enhanced by random rotation and random cropping. The speed and AP score (AP 50 and AP 50–95) were used in the comparison process. According to the experimental results, the YOLOv5s algorithm is effective in augmenting data through random crop. The AP 50 of YOLOv5s can therefore be raised from 94 % to 98%, which is adequate to meet the requirements for recognising and detecting whiteflies even though they look tiny and very similar to white spots caused by water droplets, dust on leaves, or their light reflection.

articleTitle: Volt-Var as Control Strategy of Grid-Tied Smart PV Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) poses several challenges for network control. Voltage issues are the main drawback of high DER penetration, especially in photovoltaic (PV) systems. Moreover, ensuring a balance between electricity production and consumption is still a real challenge for the power grid. In response to such constraints, PV inverters should support grid voltage. In this context, inverters play a key role in adjusting the power injected into the grid according to variations in demand and production. Conventionally, inverters were operated with a unit power factor. Still, advanced inverters, called smart inverters, can even supply reactive power to the grid to overcome voltage problems. These advanced functions enable solar PV inverters to monitor and communicate system status, automatically providing auxiliary services to the grid. Thus, advanced inverter control is essential to prevent imbalances that could lead to voltage fluctuations or grid instability. Specifically, Var-priority and Watt-priority modes were designed in the paper for a comparative study. Simulations were conducted to validate the modes' effectiveness in addressing voltage issues under grid disturbances.

articleTitle: Time Coordination Framework for Asynchronous Simulation Systems: Providing Efficient Data Exchange for Vehicle Networks Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In the realm of autonomous driving, Effective inter-vehicle communication and data exchange are crucial for developing resilient transportation systems. As cars increasingly depend on distributed networks for sharing vital information, the difficulty of synchronizing activities across asynchronous systems becomes significant. Synchronization is crucial in simulation systems because accurate time alignment directly affects the precision and reliability of the scenarios. To meet this requirement, temporal coordination frameworks are essential to ensure that vehicle systems, in both practical applications and simulations, achieve synchronization despite hardware and software constraints.

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Detection and Identification of a Photovoltaic System Based on Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The growing emphasis on sustainability and green energy in electricity generation has led researchers to focus on improving photovoltaic systems. Consequently, a reliable fault diagnosis method is crucial for protecting and maintaining the performance of PV systems. This paper introduces a fault detection approach utilizing a sliding mode observer to detect sensor faults in a standalone photovoltaic system. The method is based on residual generation, which identifies faults by comparing residuals with specific threshold values. The standalone photovoltaic test bench includes a boost converter that facilitates maximum power point tracking using the perturb and observe method for the load. Simulations are carried out in MATLAB/Simulink under stable temperature and varying irradiance conditions to evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed fault detection technique.

articleTitle: Robust Fractional Order Sliding Mode Control Against Parameter Variations with Application to SCARA Manipulator Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Fractional Order Sliding Mode Control (FO-SMC) for achieving robust motion trajectory regulation in dynamic robot systems operating under parameter uncertainties, including conditions of charge variation and overload. The proposed control strategy leverages fractional calculus to upgrade the robustness and performance of the control framework. A thorough analysis using Lyapunov's method is carried out to validate the asymptotic stability of the feedback control system. The analysis demonstrates that the proposed FO-SMC controller ensures that the tracking errors approach zero, even when faced with inherent uncertainties and disturbances in dynamic robotic environments. Simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of the suggested method in achieving precise trajectory tracking and robust performances, particularly under challenging operational conditions such as varying charge levels and overload scenarios.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Control for a Class of Nonlinear Time Delay Systems in Presence of Faults
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a fault-tolerant control (FTC) method for nonlinear systems with delays, based on Lyapunov redesign approach. The method handles actuator faults modeled as additive faults and loss of effectiveness described by a multiplicative factor. The proposed control system combines a nominal controller for normal operation and an additional component to compensate for faults, ensuring system stability. Using Lyapunov redesign principle, the stability of the system is guaranteed even under fault conditions and time delays. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the approach and demonstrate its practical use in systems where faults and delays are critical. This work provides a simple yet robust solution to improve reliability in delayed nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: Active Sensor Fault Tolerant Controller for Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In the current work, additive Fault-Tolerant Control (FTC) for wind turbine system is addressed. To design the additive control, two steps must be taken: first, the sensor fault amplitude must be accurately estimated using an Unknown Input High Gain Observer (UIHGO) with variable design parameters; second, the additive FTC law must be generated and added to the system's nominal control; the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) must be taken into account while the formulation of the nominal control law. The expression of additive control is equal to zero in the absence of a fault, while the additive control law must depend on the fault term. The method turns into an active fault-tolerant controller (AFTC) that can immediately adjust the FTC to compensate for the fault effect because the observers offered a reliable and accurate online fault estimation. The validity of the implemented controller is confirmed by the simulation results, which show how effective the recommended controller is even in the presence of faults.

articleTitle: UGV Navigation and Tracking of a Moving Target Using Artificial Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: There is much interest and research in applying Machine Learning (ML) methods for Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) applications. This work is concerned with implementing a ML system based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) for a small UGV that navigates its environment, avoids obstacles, tracks a moving target, and optimizes its path. The work includes designing and implementing a wheeled robot prototype equipped with a camera and Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensors, Arduino and Raspberry PI controllers. The research methodology was divided into three main stages. First, data was collected from the manual operation of the UGV through different environments. Then, the data was used to build and tune a Feed-Forward ANN model. Finally, the ANN model was embedded in the UGV and tested in new environments. Results show that the UGV could maneuver its environment and reach its moving target in real-time.

articleTitle: On the Finite-Time Stochastic Stability of Linear Stochastic Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of finite-time stability for time invariant linear stochastic systems. By using S-variable approach, Gronwall inequality technique and stochastic methodology in analysis, new theorem of finite-time stochastic stability is proposed and an important corollary for a specific problem is obtained. In fact, we determined sufficient conditions for achieving finite-time stochastic stability, by used matrix inequalities method. Some comparisons with the existing results are given, demonstrating that this new condition of finite-time stochastic stability are less conservative. To illustrate the effectiveness of our findings, we include two illustrative examples.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Voltage-Controlled Current Source for Wearable Bioimpedance Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) has gained prominence as a non-invasive diagnostic tool for characterizing biological tissues, offering critical insights into physiological and pathological conditions. At the core of BIS systems lies the Voltage-Controlled Current Source (VCCS), which is essential for ensuring precise and stable current delivery across varying load conditions. This paper investigates a modified dual Howland configuration with load-in-loop compensation designed for low-power applications. By operating at reduced supply voltages (5V) instead of the conventional ±12V, the proposed design addresses the limitations of existing VCCS circuits in portable and wearable medical devices. The study evaluates the performance of the proposed VCCS circuit in a wide range of frequencies (50 kHz to 1 MHz), load conditions (1000 to 18kO), and input signal types (sine, multi-sine, and sine-sweep). Key findings demonstrate stable current output, efficient power consumption, and robust performance at reduced power levels, making it suitable for bioimpedance applications requiring portable operation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Photovoltaic Water Pumping System for Sustainable Agricultural Irrigation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This study focuses on a photovoltaic water pumping system (PVWPS) designed with a three-phase induction motor (IM) and a centrifugal pump. The control strategy developed for this system includes two key components. One of these is a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) mechanism, which leverages the incremental conductance (INC) algorithm to ensure optimal power extraction from the photovoltaic array. The second controller leverages the Linearized Input-Output (LIO) method to manage the IM and the centrifugal pump, powered via a three-phase inverter. A Matlab/Simulink model was developed to validate the system's design. Simulations, conducted using real climate data from the Sidi-Bouzid region, demonstrated that the proposed PVWPS delivers enhanced performance in reference tracking, response time, torque and flux ripple reduction, current quality, and water flow rate.

articleTitle: Smart Energy Management with Integrated WSN and WMN: Advancing Efficiency and Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to provide an advanced WSN solution for power-sustainable energy management and efficient communication, integrating the latest developments from the SEMS. This work will focus on the research effort directed at improving M2M communication and integrating WSNs with wireless mobile networks, as well as addressing PAPR, energy consumption, and scalability. It now applies to real-time monitoring of power usage, room temperature, and lighting by integrating renewable resources of energy with sophisticated algorithms and sensor networks. Key results include a 16.6% saving in energy consumptions, 78% in system delay improvements, and the implementation of solar energy systems that have realized significant cost savings while assuring environmental sustainability. This work proves the ability of the approach through wide simulations and real-world deployments for scalable and eco-friendly energy management solutions. Besides, this work is closely related to worldwide goals for reduction of carbon footprints and efficient resource utilization.

articleTitle: Antenna Array Design for The Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this study the design and simulation of a microstrip antenna array for a radar application using the S-band (2 to 4 GHz) have been examined. To enhance the electrical and radiation properties of the suggested antenna, a slot is incorporated into the radiating element and a new power divider is employed. Two rows, each with four pieces, make up the planned array, which has overall measurements of 11.7 x 11.9 cm in width and length respectively. The findings indicate that at a resonance frequency of 3.76 GHz, the suggested antenna has a reflection coefficient of -34 dB. When the four-element array is assembled, the radiation gain is enhanced, reaching 6.18 dB with an efficiency of 98.66%. Furthermore, the antenna array provides complete 360° coverage, enabling omnidirectional and continuous scanning. This feature is essential for radar applications, as it ensures optimal target detection across the entire perimeter around the radar, with no dead zones or interruptions.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Linear Discrete Systems using an Interval Observer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a new prognosis approach to estimate the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of systems subject to output noise and disturbance. This approach comprises two phases: in the diagnosis phase, the fault is detected and estimated, and the prediction phase is used to predict the evolution of this fault in the future. The diagnosis step is carried out using an interval observer designed to estimate an addition to the complete state of a sensor fault on a for discrete linear systems. Next, based on an appropriate identification technique, a parametric identification is performed to estimate the future degradation until it reaches a certain failure threshold. This allows us to calculate the interval including the RUL. A numerical example illustrates the effectiveness and validity of the proposed technique

articleTitle: High-Performance Filament Strain Sensor Based on CNT-TPU-TPS with a Double Percolation Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Flexible filament sensors have gained significant attention in wearable, electronics and smart textiles. However, achieving both high sensitivity and flexibility remains challenging, due to the oversimplified thin film structure of the strain sensor. In this work, a high-performance filament strain sensor is developed using a composite of carbon nanotube (CNT), thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), and thermoplastic elastomer based-styrene (TPS). These filaments are fabricated through a combination of solution mixing and twin-screw extrusion. The sensor demonstrates excellent durability and high sensitivity, at a composition of TPS(90%)-TPU(10%) achieving a maximum gauge factor (GF) of 305.50 at 20%-40% strain, significantly outperforming the composition TPS(50%)-TPU(50%) (GF of 8.55). The results demonstrate reliable strain sensing over a broad range and stable performance over 1000 loading/unloading cycles which make it suitable for wearable electronics and human motion monitoring applications.

articleTitle: A New Efficient Hybrid Boruta-CNN-GA Technique for Predicting Financial Distress
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Financial distress prediction (FDP) has become an important area of study since it can warn the organization, investors, and creditors early. This study presents a hybrid methodology for predicting financial distress using a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a Genetic Algorithm (GA) with Boruta automated feature selection. Our CNN-GA is based on GA-based tuning of the essential CNN hyperparameters-Network depth, Dense layer activation function, Network width, and Network optimizer. We then investigate the influence of Boruta feature selection on our CNN-GA algorithm. The prediction performance is assessed using samples of firms from with samples of companies from GCC countries. The experiments in this paper use resampling with k-fold evaluation metrics, ensuring a comprehensive evaluation of our approach. The simulation results show that adopting the Boruta method has consistently boosted the accuracy of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Observer Based Fast Fixed-Time Non-Singular Terminal Sliding Mode Control of Teleoperation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper introduces a fast fixed-time non-singular terminal sliding mode control approach, utilizing a sliding mode observer, to tackle the tracking challenge in teleoperation systems. A robust fixed-time control law is formulated to achieve accurate tracking performance, effectively countering parametric uncertainties, external disturbances, and time-varying delays. Furthermore, the proposed fast fixed-time non-singular terminal sliding surface ensures convergence within a fixed time frame once the sliding condition is satisfied. To improve practical implementation, a sliding mode observer is integrated, removing the necessity for a velocity sensor. The system's stability is demonstrated through Lyapunov theory.

Author Keywords: fast fixed-time non-singular terminal sliding mode

articleTitle: 3D-HEVC Fast CCL Intra Partitioning Algorithm For Low Bitrate Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Three-Dimensional High-Efficiency Video Coding (3D-HEVC) has transformed the transmission and storage of stereoscopic and multi-view video content by efficiently encoding texture and depth information. Depth map coding is essential for synthesised views which create the 3D effect. However faces challenges in meeting the growing demand for low-bitrate encoding with faster processing times in applications like cloud streaming, low-latency broadcasting and 3D video editing software. The Coding Tree Unit (CTU) partitioning, crucial for coding efficiency, is particularly impactful for depth maps due to their sharp edges and large homogeneous regions. To address this problem, we propose a Connected Component Labeling (CCL) approach to optimise CTU partitioning for depth map coding in intra-prediction for QP pairs QP 35–42 and 40–45. By leveraging the structural properties of depth maps, CCL enables precise partitioning, thus reducing unnecessary computations and improving compression efficiency. Our method targets applications requiring efficient and fast low-bitrate encoding. Experimental results show a great reduction in encoding time with 70.64% while slightly increasing bitrate by 0.08% and managing minimal quality degradation.

articleTitle: Medical Ultrasound Image Improvement Based on Denoising Convolutional Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The challenge of enhancing ultrasound images while retaining essential features is vital in the medical field. Speckle noise significantly degrades image quality and can obscure important details. In this paper, we propose a new enhancement approach that integrates a Non-Subsampled Shearlet Transform (NSST) with a denoising autoencoder. By leveraging the capabilities of NSST for multi-scale and directional decomposition, our method effectively separates fine anatomical features from speckle noise. Our approach results in substantial speckle reduction while preserving critical details, thus enhancing the visual quality of ultrasound images. Experimental evaluations reveal the effectiveness of the proposed method in noise suppression and feature preservation, measured through various performance metrics. This innovative strategy represents a significant advancement in ultrasound image processing, with potential benefits for clinical diagnostics.

articleTitle: New Discrete Sliding Mode Control Using Fractional-Order Reaching Law for Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This work introduces a novel discrete sliding mode control approach, leveraging a fractional-order reaching law derived from the Grunwald-Letnikov framework. Specifically tailored for discrete Hammerstein nonlinear systems, the proposed reaching law replaces the classical Gao reaching law to address key limitations in robustness and convergence. By integrating fractional calculus principles, this method offers improved adaptability to system uncertainties and external disturbances, ensuring precise and stable control performance. Comprehensive simulation studies are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results demonstrate significant performance enhancements, including faster convergence, reduced chattering, and increased robustness, compared to traditional methods. These findings underscore the potential of the proposed fractional-order strategy in advancing control design for complex discrete nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Photovoltaic System Efficiency: A Comparative Analysis of Perturb&Oserve and Fuzzy Logic-based MPPT Techniques Under Uniform Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Several maximum PowerPoint Tracking (MPPT) techniques have been developed to ensure that photovoltaic (PV) systems operate at their maximum efficiency. Among these, is the Perturb and Observe (P&O) algorithm. However, despite its ease of implementation and simple structure, it has inherent algorithm limitations that affect its performance. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a fuzzy logic-based control (FLC) approach that tracks the maximum power point (MPP). a comparison between the two methods was conducted using MATLAB Simulink with 1Soltech 1STH-215-P Module under uniform conditions; the obtained results reveal that the fuzzy logic technique outperforms the P&O method in terms of efficiency.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Wide Range Fingerprinting Localization for Low-Energy Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Localization is now a popular topic in research and development. It uses various methods to locate objects in space, whether these objects are moving or static. The researchers aim to find the most accurate way to position or track these objects. GPS and similar systems provide global precision, but cannot be depended upon in indoor environments due to signal attenuation and obstacle loss, causing erroneous and poor data for the localization system. Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have enhanced techniques by employing internal signal strength in indoor environments. However, challenges remain, such as nonline-of-sight, signal variability, and energy consumption. It is important to explore other link quality metrics from the used hardware. In this paper, we intend to solve these problems using advanced Link Quality Metrics (LQM) AI-Fingerprinting based on revolutionized ML techniques, taking into consideration low energy consumption for extending the overall WSN lifetime.

articleTitle: Beamforming Techniques for High-Capacity Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This research paper presents a comparative study of analog, digital and hybrid beamforming techniques applied to two different antenna array architectures designed to operate at 143.7 GHz, a key frequency band for 5G/6G wireless communication systems. Using CST Microwave Studio, we simulated and analyzed the performance of these antenna arrays and showed the impact of different beamforming approaches on key metrics such as gain, sidelobe level and beamwidth

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of LoRaWAN Physical Transmission Parameters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is driving a technological revolution, enabling devices to communicate and interact, thereby providing a connected world of smart applications. Low-power wide-area networks (LPWANs) are a leading solution for IoT applications, requiring long-range communication with low energy consumption. Among the various LPWAN technologies, LoRaWAN stands out due to its adaptability, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for diverse use cases. LPWAN devices often provide numerous transmission parameters to ensure efficient and reliable communication. In this paper, we study the impact of LoRaWAN physical transmission parameters including Spreading Factor (SF), Bandwidth (BW), and Coding Rate (CR), on communication performance. Furthermore, the performance of LoRaWAN under a publish-subscribe architecture is evaluated using the MQTT protocol, a lightweight communication standard widely adopted in IoT systems.

articleTitle: Early Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease Using YOLOv11 Deep Learning Model in MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is an anatomical atrophy that attacks important brain regions, specially the memory and it causes the most dangerous dementia form which leads to the death. Millions of peoples in the world suffer from this disorder, and hence, many researches are conducted in order to enhance the early detection and the diagnosis of the disease. Deep learning (DL) models used in computer aided diagnosis (CAD) applications are the most effective nowadays in the classification of Alzheimer's Disease into its different progression stages. YOLO family is among the most recent deep learning architectures, and it has proven its efficiency in many computer vision applications. In this paper, we propose to train magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data for AD using YOLOv11 pre-trained model for the early detection of AD. The full brain skull was selected as a region of interest (ROI) and the dataset was acquired from Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database. Four classes of the dementia were selected, which are, ND, MoD, MD and VMD. The best precisions are obtained for ND and VMD stages with 97.6% and 91.1% respectively.

articleTitle: Fault Estimation with Practical Convergence, for Conformable Fractional Systems, Under a Disturbed Lipschitz Condition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper investigates an adaptive observer, with a practical convergence, for a generalized class of nonlinear Lipschitz conformable fractional-order systems, enabling simultaneous state and sensor fault reconstruction. While integer-order systems have been extensively studied, the development of observers for fractional-order systems, particularly those employing conformable derivatives, remains a relatively unexplored area. The proposed observer addresses this gap by handling a broader class of nonlinear systems characterized by a modified Lipschitz condition. A numerical example validates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Stereo Visual Matching for UAV Navigation: Multi-Channel Disparity Map-Based Trajectory Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Stereo vision and matching constitute a deeply researched sector within computer vision, particularly in the domains of robot and drone navigation, augmented reality, and automotive applications. Stereo matching performs more effectively in scenarios without radiometric variations compared to those with such variations present. This study delves into stereo matching techniques and proposes novel frameworks aimed at enhancing precise localization and velocity measurement of UAVs within defined boundaries. The primary focus lies on refining the accuracy of the resulting disparagement map, achieved through three key phases: pre-processing, stereo matching, and post-processing. Initially, input images undergo pre-processing using NMHE to mitigate radiometric variations. Subsequently, various features are extracted from both images during the second phase. Finally, the disparagement map undergoes post-processing to eliminate minor artifacts. Experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed modifications have significantly enhanced the performance of state-of-the-art local stereo matching algorithms and bolstered their resilience against radiometric changes.

articleTitle: Surface Roughness-Dependent Magnetic Properties in CoFeB Thin Films for Flexible Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This study explores the magnetic characteristics of CoFeB-based magnetic thin films on flexible substrates, focusing on how surface roughness affects their magnetic properties. By examining substrates such as PDMS, PI, and PEN, we observed that increased surface roughness leads to higher coercivity, enhancing sensor stability by restricting domain wall movement and resisting magnetic disturbances. The remanent magnetization to saturation magnetization ratio values for the flexible substrate were slightly lower, ranging from 72 to 60 percent of the rigid Si/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> substrate values. Still, the difference was within a manageable range. Moreover, the 4.6 - to 10.2-fold increase in coercivity on flexible substrates compared to Si/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>substrates compensates for the reduced remanent magnetization to saturation magnetization ratio, ensuring reliable performance in magnetic sensor applications. These findings highlight the potential for optimizing flexible magnetic sensors through surface engineering or multilayer designs, contributing to developing next-generation wearable and adaptable sensor devices.

articleTitle: Optimized Measurement Methods Evaluating Crosstalk in different SOI Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Crosstalk can reduce the performance of RF, analog, mixed-signal and digital integrated circuits. Measurement methods using appropriate measurement parameters to evaluate substrate crosstalk are discussed. Several layout options and technological parameters are compared. Based on these results the designer can choose and combine a set of options for more isolation of sub circuits to fulfill the requirements for the specific application. The focus is set on the different Silicon on Insulator technologies. Depending on frequency range the influence of isolation measures and their combinations is shown. The S-parameters of several test structures were measured using a vector network analyzer. The main results are differences in crosstalk between 50 MHz and 300 MHz.

articleTitle: Localization in Wireless Sensor Networks Based Enhanced Horned Lizard Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), numerous sensor nodes collect environmental data, but this data becomes meaningless without accurate locations. Therefore, in many WSN applications, including industrial, whether, military, and health, sensor node localization is crucial. It seeks to identify unknown node positions based on anchor node positions. Since traditional localization schemes, such as GPS, are not appropriate for WSN implementation because of high cost and low indoor performance, the researchers are creating alternative localization schemes. In this work, we present a nodes localization issue in WSNs based on the Enhanced Horned Lizard Optimization Algorithm (EHLOA). A comparison analysis is conducted with the standard HLOA scheme to assess the proposed EHLOA. The proposed EHLOA performs better than the standard HLOA technique by achieving faster convergence and reducing average localization error (ALE) and mean localization error (MLE).

articleTitle: Hybrid Routing in VANETs Using OLSR and Q-Learning for Enhanced Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: High node mobility, rapid topology changes provide specific challenges for vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs), which have an immediate impact on the routing protocols' performance. Traditional approaches, like the Optimized Link State Routing (OLSR) protocol, provide proactive route management but fail to fully account for critical dynamic parameters like link stability, relative vehicle speed, node distance, and bandwidth availability. This work proposes a hybrid method combining OLSR with Q-learning to facilitate real-time adaptive routing. The model leverages dynamic metrics to proactively evaluate links while employing Q-learning to optimize routing decisions based on rewards computed from performance factors like delay, packet loss rate, and link duration. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms classic OLSR. The improvements include reduced packet loss rates, increased average throughput, lower average latency, and a reduction in control overhead. These findings confirm that integrating dynamic metrics and adaptive learning effectively addresses the challenges posed by VANETs.

articleTitle: Two-Tower Neural Network for Personalizing Service Recommendation in Cloud Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Effectively recommending cloud services requires a deep understanding of both user requirements and the wide range of available cloud offerings. This paper introduces a novel two-tower neural network architecture to tackle this challenge. By leveraging the power of neural networks, we distill intricate user and cloud service information into concise vector representations, enabling the refinement of highly personalized recommendations. Our proposed two-tower architecture is specifically designed for efficient scalability within the demanding context of large-scale cloud environments. Each tower, dedicated to users and cloud services respectively, integrates a comprehensive set of relevant features and interaction data to generate dense vector embeddings. Subsequently, cloud services are ranked based on the calculated similarity between their embeddings and those of the respective users. The proposed two-tower model was evaluated on the WSdream dataset for both regression and classification tasks. Experimental results consistently demonstrated superior performance compared to state-of-the-art recommendation techniques, including k-nearest neighbors and matrix factorization.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-Beam PIFA Antenna With Modified CPW Feed for Secure Sub-6 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This work presents a broadband and low-profile printed Inverted-F antenna (PIFA). The design deploys a 1.5 mm thick FR-4 substrate with dimensions (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4 0} \times \mathbf{2 5} \mathbf{ m m}^{2}$</tex>). A broadband operation is achieved through modifying a coplanar waveguide feed (CPW). Two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda / 8$</tex> stubs are created to enhance the entire operational frequency bandwidth. The simulation result of the reflection parameter achieves about 87 % fractional bandwidth (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.05-5.2 \text{GHz}$</tex>) based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathbf{d B}$</tex> impedance bandwidth criterion. The design has total radiation efficiency above <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{7 2 \%}$</tex>. Far-field radiation patterns results show a dualpattern (pattern diversity) among excited resonance modes frequencies. Such results make the proposed antenna an excellent candidate for current secure- and selective sub-6 GHz 5G communications systems.

articleTitle: Interval Estimation of Sensor and Actuator Faults for Decoupled Multimodel
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper addresses the estimation problem of sensor and actuator faults for nonlinear systems represented by decoupled multimodel affected by unknown but bounded disturbnces and measurement noise. For this, an interval multiobserver is designed to estimate state and default vectors simultaneously. The existence of the interval observer is formulated using Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMI) to guarantee stability conditions. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is proven by simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of Antennas based on U-Shaped Slots for Wireless Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This article presents the design and analysis of a “U” slot patch antenna realized on a FR4 substrate, for dual band operation at frequencies of 2.5 GHz and 3.5 GHz. The antenna achieves a reflection coefficient (S11) of -17 dB at 2.5 GHz with a gain of 2.75 dB, and of -15 dB at 3.5 GHz with a gain of 1.55 dB. The integration of “U” slots improves impedance adaptation and allows miniaturization while maintaining acceptable performances. The low-cost use of FR4 substrate makes this design suitable for applications requiring compact and economical solutions, such as wireless communications and IoT devices. The simulation results, including S-parameters and radiation diagrams, confirm the antenna's ability to meet the requirements of dual band applications. Prospects for improvement, notably to increase the gain and bandwidth, are also discussed.

articleTitle: Impact of Electrothermal Effects on Electron and Phonon Dynamics GAAFET Transistor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Modern nanoelectronics, particularly with Metal Oxide Semiconductor (MOS) technology, has enabled the creation of smaller and faster transistors. However, these advancements also lead to significant overheating issues. This study develops a mathematical model to predict the electrothermal properties of a GAA-FET device, focusing on channel lengths of 10 and 50 nm, and evaluates its thermal stability. To achieve this objective, we analyze the limits of miniaturization, heat production in transistors, and introduce the Ballistic-Diffusive Equation (BDE) model. Using COMSOL Multiphysics to solve thermal and electrical equations, we combine the Ballistic-Diffusive and Drift-Diffusion models for a realistic thermal study of GAA-FET. The results, validated by experimental and numerical comparisons (TCAD and Monte Carlo), confirm the validity of the proposed model and the necessity of thermal studies for GAA-FET transistors.

articleTitle: An Overview of Machine Learning Approaches for ECG-Based Epileptic Seizure Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG)-based epileptic seizure detection has emerged as a promising alternative to traditional EEG monitoring, particularly for long-term ambulatory applications. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of ECG-based seizure detection methods spanning nearly five decades (1975–2024), with particular emphasis on machine learning approaches and their evolution. Through systematic analysis of 77 studies, we identify key trends in methodological development, evaluate performance across different algorithmic approaches, and provide insights into practical implementation considerations. Our analysis reveals that modern deep learning approaches achieve detection accuracies of up to 98.84%, while multimodal approaches combining ECG with other biosignals consistently out-perform single-modality methods. We present a structured framework for evaluating seizure detection algorithms and provide evidence-based recommendations for future development. Our findings indicate that careful feature selection and adaptive learning mechanisms are crucial for achieving robust performance in real-world applications.

articleTitle: A Robust Convolutional Neural Network for Electrical Impedance Tomography Image Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is a widely used non-invasive imaging method in a variety of application fields. Most EIT applications require an accurate and high-quality reconstructed inner conductivity distribution image. Several solutions have been developed for reliable EIT image reconstruction, but they still suffer from limitations such as low spatial resolution and inconsistency in real measurement scenarios. In this paper, we propose using physically based, extensive simulation data to train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model with 5-fold cross-validation. We generate a set of 10.000 data samples, which builds a comprehensive basis for its training and ensures reliability and generalization capability. The quantitative evaluation demonstrates good reconstruction performance, achieving a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0151 and an Image Correlation Coefficient (ICC) of 0.97 in the best-performing fold for the simulated data. The method's effectiveness is particularly validated through experimental measurements, where it significantly outperforms traditional Gauss-Newton reconstruction in terms of image sharpness and boundary definition. The algorithm is robust and easily applicable for EIT imaging.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Pollution Removal Efficiency in Activated Sludge Wastewater Treatment Processes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Water pollution is a growing challenge for the environment and ecosystems, necessitating management of Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs). Modeling the dynamical behaviors of these complex systems significantly affects the control and prediction performance. This study compares the performance of three widely used Activated Sludge Models (ASM1, ASM2, and ASM3) in removing key pollutants, mainly including Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD5), Total Suspended Solids (TSS), Total Nitrogen (TN), and Hydrogen potential (pH). Each model of the activated sludge process incorporates unique representation of biological and chemical processes like nitrification, denitrification, and phosphorus removal. The results demonstrate significant differences in the models' stability, sensitivity, and effectiveness under varied operational conditions. The ASM3 benchmark consistently performs well in extreme scenarios, ASM1 shows strong stability, and ASM2 balances efficiency and reliability. These findings provide actionable insights for optimizing WWTP's operations, guiding model selection based on specific treatment objectives.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of a Temperature Measurement and Control System Adapted to Gas Nanosensors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this work, we present the implementation of a temperature measurement and control system, suitable for testing new gas sensors based on metal oxide nanoparticles. The system consists of a software part, and an electronic part. In the software section, an interface was designed using graphic design software. This interface ensures the display, control and recording of the working temperature while ensuring a real-time handshake with the electronics part. The latter consists of a thermocouple type K, a heating resistor, a microcontroller-based board and a power circuit. The microcontroller-based board provides reading, local display and temperature control according to the desired set point value. The implemented control algorithm ensures real-time control parameters change according to the set point and the measuring period. A full bridge rectifier, a photocoupler, an optocoupler and a TRIAC form the power part. This system works as follows: The zero pass can be detected by the full bridge rectifier and the photocoupler, measure the temperature by the thermocouple, calculate the pulse delay with the PID control and create the pulse on the pin connected to the optocoupler that will apply a pulse to the TRIAC. This will control the amount of energy passed to the AC heating resistor. This allows to find a low static maximum error. The strength of this system is the algorithm generates, in real-time, the parameters of PID regulation, control of energy quantity using the zero-detect method, and stability over time.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fault Estimation Using a Second Order Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Ensuring great performance in the presence of sensor malfunctions requires accurate estimation of both state variables and sensor faults. The second-order sliding mode observer (2SMO) stands out for its robustness and high performance in estimating state variables, making it an effective solution for fault estimation. This paper proposes a 2SMO for the simultaneous estimation of sensor faults and state variables for discrete linear systems. The observer is designed using the Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs) approach to ensure stability. A simulation example demonstrates the efficiency and robustness of our proposed 2 SMO.

articleTitle: Focusing Properties of Dual-Square and Dualcircular Ring Arrays
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The designers of focused antennas have extensively employed the principles of antenna arrays in various attempts to improve the performance of the focused antennas. This paper presents an investigation and comparison of the properties of focused dual-ring arrays. The first one is a circular dual-ring array focused by using only one phase shifter. The second dual-ring array has a square shape, where three cases of the inner ring were considered. The CST and MATLAB software were used to investigate the designed and simulated arrays, whose outer size was fixed at 6 wavelengths. The comparison considered the results of the lateral size of the focal spot, the depth of field DOF, and the number of required phase shifters, thus reducing complexity of the feed network and cost. The circular array achieved a smaller DOF, at only one phase shifter, and a smaller number of elements. However, each of the three dual-ring square arrays achieved focused spot having a smaller transversal width, on account of a larger element number and correspondingly more phase shifters. The proposed arrays can find applications in medical imaging, hyperthermia, and industrial testing.

articleTitle: GPT Voice-Driven Natural Language Control for ArduPilot-Guided UAVs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This research work introduces a new system that utilizes Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) Large Language Models (LLMs) to enable language-based control for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The system enables nonexpert users to easily control UAVs using natural language. It integrates GPT-4o-mini model with the widely used open-source ArduPilot Software. The developed system supports both audio and written inputs and accommodates multiple languages. The LLM reasons about the request and generates the required functionality. OpenAI's API (Application Programming Interface) and Function Calling are used to implement the task.

articleTitle: Practical Observer Design for Nonlinear Systems using Caputo Fractional Derivative with Respect to Another Function
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper builds upon our prior work [23], analyzing the study of observer design for nonlinear systems utilizing the Caputo fractional derivative with respect to another function. Two critical nonlinear conditions are employed: the One-Sided Lipschitz (OSL) condition and the quasi-One-Sided Lipschitz (quasi-OSL) condition. These conditions are key to ensuring the practical stability of the system under consideration. The observer is designed with a tuned parameter, θ θ, which is chosen to be a high-gain value, effectively enlarging the set of feasible solutions. While this paper focuses on the theoretical aspects of the observer design, a numerical example remains a future objective, as the numerical approximation of the fractional derivative with respect to another function is still under development.

articleTitle: Phase Loss Detection for Three Phase AC Drives Based on Second Order Generalized Integrator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this work we present an effective approach that aims to diagnosis phase loss failures affecting three phase AC drives. The proposed approach uses Second Order Generalized Integrator (SOGI) to generate three robust fault indicators to insure effective diagnosis of the faulty phase. The detection time is equal to one cycle period of the motor stator current. Experimental results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed fault diagnosis method.

articleTitle: A Review of Effective Image Watermarking Methods With Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper reviews recent advancements in digital watermarking, focusing on transform domain techniques, perceptual mapping, and deep learningbased methods. Transform domain approaches enhance robustness against attacks, while perceptual mapping leverages the Human Visual System (HVS) to achieve high imperceptibility. Deep learning has revolutionized watermarking by automating embedding and extraction processes, improving adaptability and resilience. Additionally, hybrid methods combining these techniques are explored for their potential to unify strengths and address current limitations. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of these methods, highlights their applications, and discusses emerging trends and future directions in the field

articleTitle: Online Identification of Switched Arx-Laguerre Model Using Sliding Window Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The switched ARX-Laguerre model is a very important reduced complexity representation of a class of linear hybrid systems modeled by a switched Auto Regressive eXogenous model (SARX). This model is obtained by expanding the coefficients of every ARX sub-model on two independent Laguerre bases. Then, the SARX-Laguerre model is characterized by several Laguerre poles whose optimal values guarantee a significant parametric reduction. To identify the parameters of the SARXLaguerre model, we propose in this article an analytical method to optimize the poles and a recursive method to identify the Fourier coefficients. To create an online parametric identification algorithm of the SARX-Laguerre model we propose to realize the identification procedure on a sliding window. To evaluate the performance of the proposed online parametric identification algorithm of the SARX-Laguerre model, we use a numerical example.

articleTitle: Embedded System for Real-time Traffic Signs Recognition with Augmented Reality Implemented in ARM
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Automatic detection and recognition of traffic signs improve driving safety by alerting drivers to hazards they may not perceive. This paper proposes an embedded real-time methodology for traffic sign detection and recognition, enhanced with augmented reality to increase driver vigilance. The algorithm operates in three stages: detection, recognition, and augmented reality merging. Color filtering and shape matching are used to extract Regions Of Interest (ROIs), followed by a Haar cascade classifier for detection and categorization. The recognition stage utilizes the ORB algorithm. Implemented on an ARM platform, the system achieves 96 % accuracy in detection and recognition at 12 fps in real-world conditions.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Green Iron Doped Carbon Dot Nanoparticles for Enhanced Solar Energy Harnessing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Solar energy is a sustainable, renewable and abundant power source which is the best energy source that can replace fossil fuels and lower the impact of pollution and global warming. Solar energy is stable, independent, and safe to wide extents. Present work investigates extraction of olive oil by pressing the fresh oils to pest and then extraction of the oil from it. The extracted oil is converted into carbon dot nanoparticles via hydrothermal technique and then doped with iron metal to have more efficient activities. The synthesized nanoparticles have been confirmed by full characterization. The desired synthesized carbon quantum dot nanoparticles were evaluated for their effectiveness as solar energy harnessing agents, over three consecutive days with nearly similar weather conditions. The products (carbon dot and iron doped carbon dot) showed more efficient solar-light absorption higher than olive oil itself and showed significant difference by p-value less than 0.0001, therefore, the products can be used for solar cell applications in future.

articleTitle: Flux-Based Predictive Control for Two-Level Post-Fault Tolerant Inverters Fed IM Drives
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The three-phase four-switch (B4) inverters under predictive torque control (PTC) are often applied as fault-tolerant alternative to solve the open/short-circuit fault of the three-phase six-switch (B6) inverters. However, conventional PTC strategy suffers from the tedious adjustment of weighting factors. Therefore, predictive flux control (PFC) has been suggested based on removing the flux weighting factor from the implementation scheme. In this paper, the performance of the PFC strategy under the post fault tolerant B4 inverter fed IM drives are evaluated at transient and steady-state operations.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Circularly Polarized Multiband Antenna with High Gain for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a single-layer, high-gain, high-efficiency circularly polarized multiband antenna for wireless applications. The proposed antenna achieves significant gain and efficiency over multiple frequency bands by integrating coupled elements around the radiating patch structure. Specifically, the antenna shows a gain of 6.5 dB at 3.5 GHz, 7.2 dB at 4.5 GHz, 7.6 dB at 4.9 GHz, 10.2 dB at 5.2 GHz and 7.5 dB at 5.8 GHz. Circular polarization is successfully maintained across all operating frequencies, ensuring reliable signal transmission for wireless communication systems. In addition, the antenna has a high efficiency, with values of 85%, 93%, 94%, 95% and 87% in the respective frequency bands. The strengths of this design lie in its simple and cost-effective single layer structure, high performance across multiple bands and suitability for a wide range of wireless applications, making it an ideal solution for modern communication systems requiring compact, efficient, and multifunctional antennas.

articleTitle: Racing Into Tourism: a 3D Android Game for Promoting Erbil's Cultural Heritage
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents the development and evaluation of Tishko Car Racing, a 3D car racing game for Android devices designed to promote Erbil's cultural heritage. The primary objective is to create a visually appealing and engaging mobile game that showcases prominent landmarks in Erbil, Kurdistan, thereby contributing to the city's tourism. Utilizing Unreal Engine for core game functionality and Blender for 3D modeling, we produced optimized low-poly assets suitable for mobile devices. Adopting an Agile methodology, we designed the game loop, user interface, and essential features such as checkpoints and AI-driven opponent cars. To validate the game's performance and user experience, we conducted comprehensive experimental benchmarks across multiple devices and a user study involving 50 participants. Results indicate stable frame rates and efficient memory usage on various hardware, while the user study revealed a 72 % increase in interest to visit Erbil and high engagement levels, with 65% of players returning after one week. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of leveraging mobile gaming to enhance cultural tourism. This paper discusses the tools, workflow, experimental results, user feedback, and challenges encountered in creating a mobile-friendly 3D racing game that integrates local cultural assets.

articleTitle: A Personalized Smart Home Control System for the Elderly and People with Disabilities Using Arabic Voice Commands
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This study introduces an AI-based smart home control system designed for the elderly, disabled, and visually impaired in the Arab region. The system integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) principles, and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, enhancing hands-free control of diverse appliances using Arabic voice commands. The system includes auditory feedback for the visually impaired. The developed system is implemented for real-time operation and integrates an offline voice recognition module capable of processing commands in various Arabic dialects, including Emirati. The system demonstrated high recognition accuracy of 94.4% and seamless functionality in real-world tests. It surpasses existing solutions in linguistic adaptability, energy efficiency, and accessibility. Overall, it provides a robust foundation for a comprehensive smart home system that improves autonomy and quality of life for the elderly and people with disabilities.

articleTitle: Design of a Discrete-Time Event-Triggered Sliding Mode Control for an Input-Output Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper introduces an event-triggered sliding mode controller (ETSMC) for linear Discrete-Time (DT) systems, utilizing only an input-output (I/O) representation. To synthesis the control law, two methods are used. In the first method, the synthesis control law is considered as the sum of an equivalent and a discontinuous control terms, achieving robust performance against perturbations. However, the chattering phenomenon still exists. Therefore, in the second method, a reaching-law strategy is developed to address this problem. In order to illustrate the theoretical aspects and efficacy of this technique, a simulated example is used to evaluate the suggested strategies.

Author Keywords: Sliding mode control in discrete time

articleTitle: Study of HTLS Conductors in Iraqi Power Grid Using PLS-CADD
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: As wires are used to transmit electrical power between generation and conversion stations and up to consumption areas, transmission lines are the mainstay of the electric grid. This paper examines the possibilities of doubling the electrical transmission capacity through two main points: Firstly, The possibility of using the designs of the existing towers but substituting conventional wires with modern techniques and advanced technology of the High-Temperature Low Sag (HTLS) wires to obtain the power to be transferred, as this will save a lot of investment and operational costs in addition to the time and effort needed to complete the work. Secondly, using conventional wires with electrical capacities more significant than those currently employed in this type of line necessitates implementing an entirely new tower design. The Hurriya-Kadhimiya 132 kV transmission line was used as a case study, while the study's final findings were presented using the PLS CADD program. The application of the incredible characteristics of HTLS conductors allowed for the persistent need to increase the capacity of the transmission network on the existing power transmission line towers, which could also provide fewer conductor sags.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Influencing the Photovoltaic Panels' Reliability Based on Bow-Tie Method
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A reliability assessment methodology for photovoltaic (PV) panels linked to operating constraints using the Bow-Tie method is presented in this paper. Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) identifies potential failure modes and their causes. The analysis takes into account operating limitations as well as environmental elements including temperature, humidity, UV radiation, and dust. Then, Event Tree Analysis (ETA) is developed to illustrate the critical causes that generate the degradation of photovoltaic panels. This reliability analysis is completed by elaborate the bow-tie diagram which ensures the understanding of the consequences of the degradation causes. It also allows the implementation of control and defense barriers to extend the photovoltaic system's lifetime.
