The findings indicated that through bow-tie method, an efficient and complete assessment of the PV panel degradation linked to operating constraints can be ensured, and the suggestion of safety measures can reduce the occurrence probability of PV panel degradation.

articleTitle: Hybrid Multi-Layer Composites for Enhanced Dynamic-Static Force Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This study presents the piezoelectric and piezoresistive properties of a multilayer composite system consisting of PDMS-CNT and PDMS-BTO layers designed for dynamic and static sensing applications. The carbon nanotube (CNT) piezoresistive layer enhances the electrical conductivity and mechanical response of the composite, while the barium titanate (BTO) piezoelectric layer provides high dielectric performance and efficient voltage generation. This unique combination exploits the complementary properties of each layer to achieve a synergistic effect that surpasses traditional single-material systems. The 15% BTO-0.3% CNT configuration demonstrated optimal performance, delivering a voltage output of 2.1 V, a power density of 1.41 µW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and a noticeable change in impedance under mechanical stress. The results highlight the dual sensing capabilities of the composite, its mechanical robustness and its potential for energy harvesting, pressure sensing and structural health monitoring. This work highlights the potential of CNT-BTO composites as a platform for advancing next-generation sensing and energy systems, balancing innovation with practicality in multifunctional material design.

articleTitle: Enlarging the DA of Nonlinear Polynomial Controlled Systems via Jaya Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The last few years marked remarkable progress in developing stability analysis techniques directed at nonlinear systems. In this context, this work presents a Lyapunov-based method to estimate the region of stability of nonlinear systems. Based on LMI techniques and JAYA optimization, this work provides a maximized volume of the DA. The LMI technique is used to get the largest estimation of the DA from a given Lyapunov function and input controller. The JAYA algorithm is introduced to attain a maximized volume of the DA through an optimal selection of the Lyapunov function's parameters and input controller coefficients.

articleTitle: From M-WFrFT Towards OTFS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Orthogonal- Time-Frequency-Space (OTFS) has been suggested as a way to achieve higher performance over Delay-Doppler (DD) channels compared to the Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) system. OTFS transforms the Time-Frequency (TF) channel's domain defined in OFDM towards a Delay-Doppler (DD) channel's domain. This gives a useful tool to overcome challenges encountered in frequency-selective channels. Furthermore, an advantage is brought by the Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT) compared to the classical Fourier Transform (FT) retained in OFDM. To do that, a simplification of the generalized Weighted Fractional Fourier Transform (WFrFT) approaches led to the named FrFT. In this process, the Multi-Weighted Fractional Fourier Transform (M-WFrFT) has attracted our attention. In this paper, it will be seen how OTFS design comes as a result of M-WFrFT. It describes the design of an OTFS system based on an OFDM system. For that, the Multi-Weighted Fractional Fourier Transform is used. Simulation results demonstrate the M-WFrFT based OTFS system gives better performance compared to WFrFT-OTFS system.

articleTitle: High Performance for PV Panel System Based on Optimal Cooling Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In terms of normalized electrical power generation, effectiveness ratio, and module efficiency, this study demonstrates the excellent efficiency of photovoltaic solar cells with cooling. The study's goal is to use a hybrid cooling system to increase the efficiency, performance, and creation of an affordable cooling system. The performance of two solar modules, one cooled and one not, was investigated and compared When the temperature of the PV panels hits its Maximum Allowable Temperature (MAT), a mathematical model is employed to determine when to begin cooling them. Based on the suggested cooling system, a cooling system has been built to find out how long it requires to cool lower the photovoltaic panels to their usual operational temperature, i.e., 35 C. When compared to the uncooled module, the cooled module had 7.2% and 6% greater electrical performance and effectiveness ratio, respectively. The findings of this study demonstrate the significance and practicality of the research.

articleTitle: Modal Interaction for Enhanced Gas Sensing in NEMS Using Roof-Tilting Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper introduces a highly sensitive and stable Nanoelectromechanical Systems (NEMS) sensor that overcomes the challenges faced by conventional sensors in detecting low gas concentrations while minimizing fluctuations caused by temperature variations, excitation amplitude shifts, and Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). By leveraging a slope-based detection mechanism driven by modal interactions, the sensor effectively mitigates the impact of slow excitation amplitude variations. The design features a nano cantilever, a 200 nm-thick Zinc Oxide (ZnO) layer, which serves as both the structural and sensing element. This configuration enables precise angle tilts corresponding to specific gas concentrations, achieving detection sensitivity beyond the capabilities of traditional sensors. Furthermore, the proposed sensor exhibits high linearity over a broad range of mass perturbations and maintains robust performance under varying environmental temperatures, making it well-suited for diverse engineering applications.

articleTitle: Insights from TCAD Simulation for Enhancing Performances of Tunable Organic Light-Emitting Diodes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) technology provides benefits such as excellent color reproduction and energy efficiency. Color tuning is still a challenge under investigation. Hence, various solutions aim to get more versatile color control OLED are proposed. This paper is focused on two approaches to develop color-tunable OLEDs (CT-OLEDs). More specifically, it investigates the impact of the emissive layer thickness (EML) and the integration of a holeblocking layer (HBL) on the OLEDs’ performances. Silvaco TCAD is used to investigate and evaluate the electroluminescence (EL) spectrum based on these two approaches. Results clearly show that color modulation can be controlled in a precise and efficient manner without any loss of time and materials during the experimentation. Furthermore, color modulation is possible for the same device via multiple approaches.

articleTitle: Chemical Reactor Identification: a Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper proposes a comparative study for the identification results of a chemical system. It consists in estimating the dynamic behavior of the process using PieceWise AutoRegressive eXogenous (PWARX) models, multimodel and classical ARX approaches. The determination of a PWARX hybrid model is carried out by the Outer Bounding Ellipsoid (OBE) algorithm. The latter is applied for system identification in cases where the disturbances are bounded. So, this work deals with the experimental application of OBE method in order to estimate the behavior of studied system with piecewise affine hybrid model. The obtained results are then compared with two existing approaches, showing that modeling the nonlinear chemical process with PWARX systems provides the best results in terms of precision.

articleTitle: Energy Management of a Hybrid Generator (PV and WT) for a Domestic Load Connected to the STEG Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Today, electrical energy plays a central role in all human and industrial activities, due to its diversity and scale. So, in order to reduce our ecological footprint, combat climate change and preserve the planet's biodiversity, it is imperative to move towards sustainable development. Currently, there is a growing trend towards the use of renewable sources to supply both isolated sites and those connected to the electricity grid. The use of a hybrid system consisting of a photovoltaic generator and a wind turbine offers a better solution, especially for unconnected sites far from the grid. This type of promising system plays an essential role in the field of renewable energy. To boost energy production, cover energy demand during peak consumption in the summer season and supply its customers' energy needs, STEG Tunisia is pushing to use renewable energies such as photovoltaics connected to their network. Indeed, STEG Tunisia allows renewable generators to be interconnected to their network in order to inj ect excess production. This option minimizes energy costs for subscribers, which in turn boosts electricity production on the grid. The work objective is to design the model of the system studied and the simulation of this autonomous system connected to the STEG grid. This system is regulated by a supervision strategy to command the movement of electricity around the different units and the household load. The concept and validation of this work were carried out using MATLAB software. The outcomes confirm the significance of the created work.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Low-voltage Low-power CMOS Dynamic Comparator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: High-speed and low-voltage comparators are considered basic building blocks for analogue-to-digital converters. This paper presents a dynamic two-stage comparator that significantly improves the performance of existing designs in the literature, particularly in terms of speed and power consumption. The comparator features a modified preamplifier stage with two interconnected control transistors, which improve its performance by reducing delay and increasing speed. Simulations using the Cadence tool in a 90 nm CMOS process show a delay of 257 ps and a power consumption of just 16.8 nW at a supply voltage of 0.75 V, highlighting its robustness compared with conventional comparators.

articleTitle: Feature Engineering for Accurate Low-Power Electrical Impedance Tomography in Hand Sign Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Achieving high classification accuracy from raw measurements in Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) for hand sign recognition is a significant challenge due to the inherent ill-posed nature of the corresponding inverse problem to solve. Energy consumption is an issue, especially for wearable devices, so there is a growing preference to measure EIT with fewer electrodes or fewer current injections. In a previous study, we demonstrated that an 8-electrode hand gesture recognition system could achieve high accuracy with only 5 current injections instead of 8, resulting in significant power savings. In this study, we investigate feature extraction and selection techniques to improve the classification accuracy in the low-power EIT system based on less measurements. We evaluate the performance of 12 statistical features by analyzing the Feature Importance (FI) and identify 8 features with non-zero values: WL, MAV, Kurtosis, VORDER, DASDV, RMS, P2P and VAR. Using K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), a comparative classification is performed using subsets of the best ranked features ranging from 2 to 8. Compared to the 96% accuracy achieved with raw data, our solution achieves 99.8% accuracy with the 8 extracted features. The results show that feature engineering significantly improves classification accuracy compared to the use of raw data.

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Estimation and Ftc Design for Fractional Linear Systems Using the Conformable Derivative
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, Fault Tolerant Control (FTC) for fractional-order systems (FOS) has not received as much attention in the literature as it has for standard integer-order systems. This work aims to bridge that gap. We propose a practical approach to fault estimation and fault-tolerant control (FTC) specifically designed for linear (FOS) with sensor failures. Our method leverages fractional exponential stability within the Lyapunov framework and employs the Conformable formulation of fractional derivatives. Notably, the primary contribution of this paper is the first application of the Conformable fractional derivative (CFD) in the context of (FTC). To accurately estimate states and faults, the proposed approach utilizes an observer coupled with a customized adaptation law. To validate our theoretical contributions, we present a detailed simulation of a numerical case study.

articleTitle: Python as a Tool in Feedback Control System Analysis and Design
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Feedback control system analysis and design is a vital part of any engineering education. The most commonly applied software solutions related to it are Matlab together with Simulink. In recent years, especially due to an ever-increasing importance of artificial intelligence in all aspects of our life, Python seems to be the programming language of choice in many universities. For this reason there seems to be pressure on Control Engineering society to also adopt Python in both educational and industrial environment. Consequently, a decision was made to present current state of the art in Python libraries that try to offer Matlab/Simulik capabilities for Python users. In this paper, a critical assessment will be made together with some examples being presented.

articleTitle: Sensor Design Based on MSL Coupled with HCSRR-Loaded Ground Plane for Material Characterization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Material characterization utilizing electromagnetic planar sensors is a promising area within modern sensing technology. This work introduces a novel sensor design based on a microstrip line (MSL) structure coupled with three hexagonal-shaped complementary split-ring resonators (HCSRR) etched onto the ground plane. The primary purpose of the proposed sensor is to measure the dielectric constant of the material under test (MUT). The MSL-HCSRR sensor is specifically engineered to operate within the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) frequency band centered at 2.4 GHz. The total dimensions of the sensor structure are optimized to 0.35 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.16 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.01 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The interaction of electromagnetic waves with the MUT induces a shift in resonant frequencies, utilized for material characterization. The proposed MSL-HCSRR configuration exhibits an E-field distribution of about 1.15 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> V/m and hence, enhances the sensitivity of the sensor by inducing a resonance response that is influenced by the changing dielectric properties of the MUT. This approach enables precise and reliable characterization of materials, particularly those with varying dielectric constants.

articleTitle: Design of Hysteresis Band Current Control for Induction Motor Drive Powered by Wind Energy Source
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The system uses wind energy as its power source and is a three-phase inverter controlled by hysteresis current. Through a rectifier circuit, a wind turbine generator provides the three-phase inverter's input DC power. The purpose of a capacitor is to lessen the oscillation of the rectifier's DC voltage output. The hysteresis current control approach is used to generate the inverter's switching pulses. This system has the advantage of reducing low frequency harmonics and controlling the fundamental amplitude based on frequency to the hysteresis current control. MATLAB simulations are used to validate the system's outputs.

articleTitle: Prediction of Vertebral Fracture Risk Using Support Vector Machine Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Since osteoporosis is a widespread disease characterized by low bone density and bone tissue structural deterioration, early diagnosis of this pathology is then essential. The purpose of this work is to provide a support vector machine (SVM) multi descriptor model for fracture risk prediction based on CT Scan and Dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) input of cadaveric lumbar vertebrae. More specifically, the aim is to test the SVM learning by combining biomechanical characteristics such as “fracture stresses” and microarchitectural features with Bone Mineral Density (BMD). The contribution of microarchitectural parameters allowed the model to better capture essential aspects of bone quality overlooked by conventional techniques like DXA. The experimental results show that the proposed method can detect vertebral fracture risk with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhanced Performance of Microstrip Antenna Array for the Wifi Application
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this paper, the design of WiFi antenna array at 2.4 GHz is presented. To overcome the limitations in electrical characteristics, in order to enhance impedance matching, a slot approach was first used, yielding a gain at 2.87 dBi and a return loss S11 at -17.59 dB. Further modifications are used, including chamfered edges and an additional rectangular element, resulted in an enhanced S11 at-45.17 dB and a gain at 3.06 dBi, suggesting improved radiation efficiency and impedance. After that, the 2x2 antenna array was added to boost gain even further, resulting in an S11 at -30.08 dB and a gain at 6.16 dBi. This iterative design process demonstrates the potential of combined structural refinements and array techniques to enhance the performance of proposed antenna for wireless applications.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Spreading Factor Adjustment Algorithm for LoRa Sensors Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic algorithm for a wireless sensor network (WSN) that utilizes Long Range (LoRa) modulation at a frequency of 2.4 GHz. The algorithm aims to optimize the throughput of the WSN by dynamically adjusting the spreading factor (SF) of each sensor node in response to real-time channel conditions and traffic demands. In high-traffic situations, the algorithm employs channel activity detection (CAD) during the preamble period to select the appropriate SF by adjusting the transmitter's SF. This selection process is based on the knowledge of its own SF for each LoRa sensor node, which is determined by its coverage radius from the LoRa master node. The proposed algorithm, termed Dynamic SF Adjustment using Channel Activity Detection (DySFCAD), operates without the need for packet exchanges. It functions in both ascending and descending modes. We evaluate the throughput performance of the LoRa-WSN under various scenarios, taking into account different configurations of the LoRa parameters.

articleTitle: Accuracy Study Based on Different Preprocessing Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: With the ever-increasing data in the world, artificial intelligence (AI) is predicted to be an essential tool for converting huge data into meaningful data. The goals of machine learning (ML) are to identify complicated patterns in multi-dimensional data and utilize uncovered patterns to classify processes or predict data. Prediction accuracy is the accustomed measure of success in ML applications. In this paper, the effect of using a machine learning approach on accuracy value is studied. We compared three feature selection algorithms, namely IndFeat, MRMR, and ANOVA algorithms. The SVM classifier is applied to the selected features in order to compare the three algorithms and examine the effect of data reduction on the accuracy value. The simulation results showed that the ANOVA algorithm is better than the MRMR and IndFeat algorithms.

articleTitle: Development and Validation of a Low-Cost, Low-Power Patient Monitoring System Using AmBC Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The implementation of Patient Monitoring (PM) in the intensive care unit (ICU), intensive coronary care unit (ICCU) and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), as well as in a paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) are currently imposes a significantly high cost of investment. According to studies conducted, there are three main parameters required to be measured, which are heart rate (BPM), oxygen saturation (SPO2), Heartbeat (ECG or EKG) and body temperature (T). These are highly needed by the medical personnel to monitor in order to determine patient's vital state. The low-cost patient monitor prototype (named Patient Monitor 4 Parameters or PM4P) was developed using Node MCU ESP8266 platform. To measure the parameters, three types of sensor modules were chosen, namely DS18B20 for gathering the body temperature data, AD8232 for gathering heartbeat data and MAX30100 for gathering heart rate and oxygen saturation data. The prototyping process also included fixation and finalization of electrical circuit on a printed circuit board (PCB). The PM4P underwent extensive validation process by comparing it to the real industrial PM made by healthcare equipment industry. The comparison was done over data gathered by both system that were conducting the same measurement runs in parallel. Results of validation indicates that the low-cost and low power patient monitor prototype can be integrated in the development of a new approach based on backscatter communication over 5G and Wi-Fi network.

articleTitle: Explainable Pre-Trained Models for Skin Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Skin cancers represent a significant health issue, posing considerable challenges in early detection and accurate classification. This study investigated the effectiveness of Deep Learning (DL) models for skin cancers classification using dermoscopic images. Two pre-trained models, DenseNet169 and VGG16, were employed. The DenseNet169 model delivered the highest accuracy, reaching 90.61% while, the VGG16 model achieved an accuracy of 84.24%. The two models were assessed using key performance metrics to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of their effectiveness and overall performance. This analysis provided significant insights on various aspects of each model, allowing a detailed comparison. It also provided a clearer comprehension of the strengths and weaknesses of both models, aiding in informed decision-making and driving further optimization. In addition, three explainable AI (XAI) techniques were applied to deliver perceptions into the decision-making process. These techniques enhance model interpretability by emphasizing the regions of the input images that contribute most to the classification decision, thus improving the transparency and reliability of the model's predictions. Reliable skin cancer classification has the potential to assist healthcare specialists, particularly dermatologists, in making early diagnoses, facilitating timely interventions, and ultimately improving patient outcomes. This study offers valuable contributions for enhancing skin cancer detection and classification, supporting accurate diagnosis and treatment development for medical practitioners.

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival Estimation Using Hybrid CNN-GRU
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a novel hybrid deep-learning network for accurate direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. The proposed method leverages the columns of the covariance matrix to construct a model-assisted deep-learning framework, integrating the strengths of the Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) and the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). This hybrid architecture utilizes selected elements from the received signal's covariance matrix as input features, while the corresponding angles serve as labels for training. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing deep learning approaches, showcasing superior performance across various conditions.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Low-Voltage Binary Search Analog-to-Digital Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced design for a low-voltage, low-power, 3-bit binary-search analog-to-digital converter (ADC), focusing on optimizing the performance of the comparator used in fast ADC circuits. The proposed solution features a modified dual-tail comparator, designed for lower technology nodes and reduced supply voltage, improving overall efficiency. Unlike traditional architectures that require 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>-1 comparators, the new design reduces the number of comparators needed, 2N-1, achieving better resource utilization. The system includes a sample-and-hold circuit, an encoder, a D-latch, five voltage comparators, and two logic gates. Simulation results using Cadence with 90 nm CMOS technology at a supply voltage of 0.75 V reveal exceptional efficiency, with a power consumption of just 39.9 µW and a bandwidth of 1.11 GHz, making it suitable for next-generation high-performance, low-power ADC applications.

articleTitle: Wideband Polarizer Using Dielectric Slabs with Periodic Rings for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A wideband polarizer is presented using an array of dielectric slabs for K-band applications, such as satellite communications. To build the polarizer, a unit cell consisting of a single dielectric slab is first designed and simulated to study the polarization conversion performance. The incident linearly polarized plane wave is modelled by two orthogonal components transmitted from one port, and the phase shift between them is determined at the second port of the unit cell. Concentric conducting rings are added on both sides of the slab to improve impedance matching and thus widen the bandwidth. The proposed polarizer, formed of an array of dielectric slabs, is investigated using the CST software assuming an operation frequency of 20 GHz. The simulated results demonstrate that linear to circular polarization conversion is achieved over a fractional bandwidth of 43% extending from 15.8 to 24.5 GHz, while impedance matching is achieved across a 200% fractional bandwidth. Furthermore, the insertion loss associated with implementing the polarizer layer remains below 0.5 dB throughout the frequency range. The proposed polarizer is a suitable candidate for a linear polarized antenna array designed for K-band applications that use circular polarization.

articleTitle: IoT and AI-Driven Smart Power Management System for Optimizing Resource Usage in Smart Buildings: The Faculty of Engineering at the Hashemite University Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper introduces an IoT and AI-Driven power management framework designed to optimize energy consumption and promote sustainability in smart buildings. The system integrates IoT technologies, smart metering, renewable solar energy, and the ThingWorx IoT platform to enable real-time monitoring, dynamic control, and efficient energy management. By leveraging both rule-based control algorithms and AI-driven forecasting, the proposed solution adaptively operates HVAC, lighting, and other energy-intensive processes in response to sensor data and predictive analytics. The proposed solution aims to enhance resource efficiency, reduce operational costs, and contribute to sustainable infrastructure development, providing a scalable model for energy optimization in institutional settings.

articleTitle: Optimal Performance of SCARA Robot System for Handling Objects Based on Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper discusses the use of image processing to improve object handling in the SCARA robot system. The proposed approach aims to achieve faster and safer movement of the SCARA robot arm for object handling. During the experiment, the optimal performance modification determines the subsystem required to accommodate and compensate for the system's image processing capability. In general, images are processed at lower speeds, as higher speeds could potentially damage the object during system transportation. The results of the proposed approach indicate the development of new object-handling techniques for SCARA robot movements by introducing visual feedback to display and control objects. To improve object handling by the SCARA robot, several parameters in the image are described in the subsequent process. This new application of the SCARA robot system is significant, as the collision-free machine modifications emphasize the safety of the working setup. It was found that the precise manipulation of the SCARA robot when handling objects in open-loop control lacks sufficient technical representation.

articleTitle: Robust Stability and Observability Analysis of Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This work focuses on the analysis of uncertain neutral time-delay systems, which involve delays in both the state and its derivatives. Our study aims to investigate the stability and observability of transmission lines under both certain and uncertain conditions. To achieve this, we employ the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional as a key analytical tool. By solving linear matrix inequalities (LMI) and applying optimization theory, we derive new criteria for ensuring stability and observability. These criteria are then validated through simulation results, demon-strating the practical applicability of our theoretical findings. Our approach not only enhances the understanding of transmission line dynamics but also provides robust methodologies for ensuring system reliability and performance.

articleTitle: Exploiting Outdoor-Induced Vibrations at Castello Normanno-Svevo Aci Castello
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper investigates the vibrations at Castello Normanno-Svevo Aci Castello in Catania, Italy. The study is conducted within the context of examining vibration levels and frequency distribution in environments of historical and artistic significance. The objectives focus on two key aspects related to cultural heritage: measuring mechanical vibrations for the preventive conservation of artifacts and structures of historical and artistic interest and exploring the potential use of such kinetic energy to power autonomous systems. This paper specifically focuses on a preliminary study of the outdoor environment. Based on the vibrational analysis, the successive aim is to develop optimized MEMS and generate transducers tailored to the specific context and area of interest. The analysis concentrated on time-domain signals along the X, Y, and Z axes, with an in-depth examination of the Z axis using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Power Spectral Density (PSD). The results revealed consistent vibration patterns across all three axes, with the vertical axis (Z) being more significantly influenced by outdoor-induced vibrations, primarily caused by sea movements and wind. The findings illustrate the vibration levels at this location and the relevant spectral distribution for future applications in designing optimized electromechanical converters, energy harvesting systems, and autonomous measurement nodes suitable for operation in this environment.

articleTitle: Brain MRI Hippocompus Segmentation for Alzheimer's Disease Based on Linknet Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a neurological disorder marked by progressive cognitive decline and memory loss due to brain cell degeneration. This study aims to segment the hippocampus in MRI scans of patients with Alzheimer's disease using a deep learning approach. The study employs a LinkuNet convolutional neural network architecture based on fully convolutationl in the decoder for hippocampus segmentation on MRI data. The model was trained and tested using MRI scans from 100 and 35 patients, respectively, from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative dataset. The performance of the automatic segmentation was assessed by comparing it to manual segmentation using similarity metrics. The segmentation yielded optimal results after 10 iterations. The method achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 9938, F1_score of 0.9938, and valid loss of 0.0462 for the test set. The findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed method for effective hippocampus segmentation. The findings demonstrate the potential of the LinkNet-based model as a robust tool for clinical applications in Alzheimer's disease research and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Adaptive Multiobjective General Predictive Controller for a Class of Uncertain Switched Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The study established within the framework of this paper concerns the issues of a class of systems having a discrete dynamic that changes its model. More precisely, the focus is on those characterized by unpredictable changing modes. This type of system is known as switched system. In this context, the paper examines the design issue of an appropriate predictive control law capable of stabilizing the system by tracking a variable reference. The control law within the framework of the current paper is designed as a dynamic optimal solution of a multi-objective problem, which considers the dynamics of all modes. To evaluate and examine the performance of the developed control scheme, several simulation tests were conducted using a benchmark example. The obtained results show that the realized method effectively addresses the control issues of the considered system class under general reference tracking.

articleTitle: State of Charge Estimation of Lithium-ion Batteries Using Long Short Term Memory Network in Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Precise State-of-Charge (SoC) estimation is crucial for accurate electric vehicle range prediction and efficient battery charge management. This paper explores a computationally efficient machine learning approach to address SoC-estimation-related issues. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is utilized for predicting the SoC of lithiumion batteries, leveraging real-time data on temperature, voltage and current. The proposed LSTM model demonstrates remarkable performance, achieving a mean absolute error of 1.02%, as well as a 1.35% root mean squared error at 25°C, while ensuring low computational overhead, making it suitable for practical implementation in Battery Management Systems (BMSs). This work lays a solid foundation for future advancements in BMS design, offering significant improvements in SoC prediction accuracy, reliability and efficiency. The findings suggest that LSTM networks can effectively model the complex dynamics of battery behavior, even when having varied operational conditions.

articleTitle: Pothole Detection Under Various Weather Conditions Using YOLOv9
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Potholes pose significant dangers on roads, leading to substantial damage to vehicles, causing accidents, and increasing maintenance costs for authorities. Accurate and timely detection of potholes is crucial for effective road maintenance and repair. However, this task is challenging, especially under varying weather conditions. Rain, snow, and fog can obscure sensors and cameras, making it difficult to capture clear images of the road surface. Additionally, nighttime and shadows can further reduce the visibility of potholes. In this paper, we propose a pothole detection system that operates effectively under diverse weather conditions using YOLOv9, a real-time object detection algorithm. Our approach was trained and evaluated on a dataset of images generated under different weather scenarios. The resulting model achieved a precision of 0.807, a recall of 0.759, a mAP50 of 0.829, and a mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>-<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">95</inf> of 0.551.

articleTitle: Advancing Emotion Recognition through LLaMA3 and LoRA Fine-Tuning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Emotion recognition from text is a key task in natural language processing (NLP), with applications ranging from interactive chat systems and mental health detection to consumer feedback analysis. While various machine learning and deep learning techniques have been explored, the success of Large Language Models (LLMs) presents new opportunities revolutionizing how we interact with text. In this study, we harness LLaMA-3-8B for this task by applying LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation), a highly effective fine-tuning technique that reduces computational and memory costs while maintaining high performance. Experiments on the ISEAR, Emotion for NLP and SemEval 2019 datasets demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency over traditional approaches. This work highlights the potential of Llama-3-8B, combined with LoRA, to excel in complex language understanding tasks, particularly in emotion recognition.

articleTitle: DITHER: Digital Twin for Energy Estimation of Heterogeneous Swarm of Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The increasing adoption of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in industrial applications such as construction inspection and infrastructure monitoring necessitates the development of efficient path planning and energy management strategies. This paper presents DITER, a Digital Twin system designed for energy consumption profiling and management in UAV-based construction inspection tasks. The proposed system integrates real-time data acquisition, energy consumption profiling, and path optimization using a hybrid approach combining path planning and energy efficiency models. Experiments conducted with a DJI Tello UAV show that the digital twin framework facilitate UAV operational in complex inspection tasks by balancing energy consumption and path length. The proposed system can be extended to support multi-UA V collaborative operations in future research.

articleTitle: Interval Cascade State Observer Design Method for Linear Delayed Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative LMI-based approach for creating an interval cascade state observer specifically designed for linear continuous systems with delays. Utilizing interval observation methods, the proposed technique effectively tackles the issues caused by time delays in system dynamics, ensuring reliable state estimation. The stability of the system is thoroughly examined using Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals, which provide sufficient conditions for the boundedness of estimation errors. The observer's robustness is tested under various disturbances, demonstrating its resilience in different scenarios. Theoretical findings are supported by simulation results, high-lighting the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed observer for systems with time delays.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of ANFIS and DRL Based Speed Controllers for Sensorless Drives
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) are of great interest in automation and robotics applications due to their small size, high efficiency, and low maintenance requirements. However, these motors face challenges in controlling their speed and position, such as precise rotor detection. This situation is essential in many Industrial applications. Conventional controllers such as PID controllers are commonly used, but their performance is often affected by changes in system dynamics, necessitating updating of controller parameters based on the accurate mathematical model of the motor. This research aims to investigate several intelligent control strategies that do not rely on the mathematical model of the motor. The performance of the drive system will be evaluated using three intelligent controllers: a neural network controller, a neural fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) controller, and a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) controller. The performance of these smart controllers will be compared with that of the PID controller. The results presented in this paper demonstrate the ability of the proposed smart controllers to regulate the speed of PMSMs compared to a PID controller. Specifically, the ANFIS-based controller shows the best performance in terms of maximum overshoot, while the DRL controller demonstrates the best settling time.

articleTitle: Advancing Color Classification: Integrating Optic Fiber Sensing and LED Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to color properties classification using an optic fiber HFBR-0500Z Series coupled with a white LED. The sensor system is designed to categorize colors based on their brightness levels, offering a versatile and cost-effective solution for diverse industries. The research focuses on testing the sensor system on the Munsell soil color chart for soil analysis. Through comprehensive experimentation and evaluation, our sensor system demonstrates robustness and accuracy in color classification across different environments and applications. This research contributes to advancing color classification technology, offering practical solutions for improving efficiency, precision, and innovation in various fields.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Control of a Two-Tank System Using Lyapunov Redesign
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The design of a stabilizing controller for uncertain nonlinear systems with control constraints is a challenging problem. This paper proposes a fault-tolerant control method for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with actuator faults, based on the Lyapunov redesign principle. First, an assumption is introduced to design the control of the nominal system. Then, a new control law is proposed to address the challenges posed by actuator faults and system uncertainties. It is shown that both actuator faults and uncertainties can be completely compensated by the proposed nonlinear controller. Finally, the method is applied to a two-tank system to demonstrate its effectiveness in a practical stabilization and control context.

articleTitle: Partial Shading of Solar Panels: Theoretical Analysis; MATLAB Modeling; and Remedies
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The effects of partial shading can be severe, even when only a small fraction of the panel is shaded. This phenomenon can lead to several issues. Reduced Power Output: As mentioned earlier, solar cells are typically connected in series, meaning that the current flowing through the entire string is limited by the lowest-performing cell. A shaded cell acts as a bottleneck, reducing the current in the entire panel and thereby decreasing its output power. In extreme cases, the shaded cell can even reverse current flow, leading to energy loss. Hot Spots and Damage: Partial shading can create “hot spots” on the panel, where the shaded cells overheat due to the backflow of current. These hot spots can cause permanent damage to the solar panel, significantly reducing its lifespan. Prolonged exposure to these conditions may cause the affected cells to fail entirely, which can be costly to replace.

articleTitle: Path Planning for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles in Complex Environments Based on a PRM* Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper proposes a Probabilistic Roadmap (PRM) planner for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) navigating in complex 3D environments. An improved version of PRM algorithms, called PRM*, is introduced to improve the capabilities of nodes specification, edges construction, and graph creation. For implementation, a pseudo-code for the proposed PRM* planner is provided. Numerical simulations are performed in different scenarios with increasing number of static obstacles and complexity. Evaluations of the generated collision-free paths are carried out using the Straight-Line Rate (SLR) and Computational Time (CT) metrics. Analyses and comparisons are performed to validate the significance and superiority of the proposed PRM* planner. Demonstrative results show that the PRM* algorithm outperforms the ordinary PRM one in terms of path compactness, smoothness, and collision avoidance.

articleTitle: Medical Images Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The World Health Organization has announced the most recent coronavirus-related disease, Covid-19 (Coronavirus Disease-2019), a pandemic. In addition, the worldwide lockdown implementation has made the whole globe to have millions of people dead. Added to the fact of being extremely contagious, this virus has a high mortality rate. In other words, it puts pressure on the healthcare system because of infecting many individuals. Therefore, identifying Covid-19 has become critical. In fact, this study aims to apply X-ray as well as Computed Tomography (CT) augmented datasets in order to realize a deep learning technique based on the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to immediately detect and diagnose Covid-19. With an efficient loss function, we have typically developed our deep learning model performance. Furthermore, the proposed system carried out high Covid-19 detection performance with a significant accuracy.

articleTitle: Interval Observer Design Method for Uncertain Linear Impulsive Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of interval state observers for uncertain linear im-pulsive systems subject to bounded disturbances and parametric uncertainties. According to positive systems theory, an hybrid interval observer is designed to give upper and lower bounds of the state. The design problem is formulated as Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) and the efficiencies of the proposed approach are validated through numerical simulations, demonstrating its robustness against bounded uncertainties and disturbances.

articleTitle: “Living” First-Order High-Pass Filter Based on Sansevieria and Lucky Bamboo Plants
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This study explores plant-based living electronic systems, aiming to create biodegradable solutions that also contribute to CO2 absorption from the environment. Specifically, it investigates the use of plant stems to develop eco-friendly circuit components for sensor signal conditioning. Electrical characterization was conducted on the stems of Sansevieria cylindrica and Dracaena sanderiana, analyzing their capacitive and resistive properties in the laboratory. The experimental findings were compared with a mathematical model for dielectric materials, emphasizing how capacitance changes with the frequency of the input voltage signal (20 Hz to 200 kHz) and the distance between electrodes applied to the plant. A passive first-order high-pass filter was then designed and tested using these stems. The optimal configuration was determined based on the measured electrical properties, resulting in a filter capable of effectively attenuating low-frequency signals. This research demonstrates the feasibility of developing fully biodegradable signal conditioning systems, with designs adaptable to the geometric features of different plant stems.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Lithium-Ion Battery Considering the Effect of SOC and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: The use of lithium-ion batteries (LIB) is common in portable devices, electric vehicles, and aerospace applications thanks to their considerable amount of energy density, compact size, as well as the low maintenance costs. These advantages make them a key technology in promoting sustain ability and combating climate change. A reliable lithium-ion battery (LIB) model is essential for accurately estimating key parameters such as voltage and state of charge. Developing an efficient and precise battery models are considered vital, as they account for various influencing factors. A battery model was developed in this study, using MATLAB/Simulink, focusing on the effects of temperature and SOC. The model is explained, developed, and validated against experimental data, measuring voltage, SOC, and current under varying temperature conditions. Although this model currently considers only SOC and temperature, it can be extended to include additional factors.

articleTitle: Modeling the Maintenance Operation of a Car Production Workshop Using Arena
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In this article, we present the development and analysis of a global model for an automotive production system, focusing on the integration of corrective and preventive maintenance strategies. Using Arena software, we simulate normal system operation, focusing on maintenance operations and strategic decisions. This model provides a valuable reference for understanding standard system behavior, making it easier to optimize maintenance strategies. The results obtained demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating preventive and corrective maintenance approaches, helping to improve the reliability and efficiency of production systems.

articleTitle: State Estimation Using Interval Observer for MIMO Nonlinear System with Noisy Outputs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A study of the state estimation for a class of MIMO nonlinear systems that are uniformly observed with noisy outputs is considered. The main contribution of this paper is to make the evidence of the robustness of the interval observer to the external noises that are added to the measured system outputs. To prove the good behavior of the proposed observer in terms of good estimation with its insensitivity with respect to noise measurements, simulation results applied to class of nonlinear systems are given.

articleTitle: 3D FEA and Broken Magnet Study of PMSM Topologies for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This work present the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) based investigation and a study of the performances of the Permanent Magnets Synchronous Machines (PMSMs) for the case of normal and in failure conditions. the work for different PMSM topologies highlight the rotor topology choice influence on the machine performances, the torque and the cogging torque analysis for the designed machines represent an objective for a smooth torque especially for the Electric Vehicle (EV) and for hybrid propulsion application, for this goal two topologies of PMSM are implemented and studied for normal condition and the case when we have a broken magnet rotors the diagnosis of the different PMSM topologies is obtained with 3D transient FEA.

articleTitle: A Novel Hardware Approach to Image Encryption Using Chaotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a novel chaotic pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) architecture that integrates the XoShiRo128++ algorithm with a chaotic logistic map, combined with an XOR operation using a Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR). The hybrid PRNG harnesses the high statistical quality of XoShiRo128++ and the sensitivity of chaotic systems to initial conditions, producing robust and unpredictable sequences. This generator is applied to image encryption using the XOR operation, and its performance and security are thoroughly evaluated. The hardware implementation is carried out on a Zybo Z7 board from the Zynq-7000 family, a resource-constrained FPGA platform. The performance analysis encompasses FPGA resource utilization, timing efficiency, and image-based metrics such as entropy and pixel correlation. The results demonstrate that the proposed chaotic PRNG provides a secure and efficient encryption system, making it highly suitable for resource-limited environments and promising for lightweight cryptographic applications.

articleTitle: Improving Energy Efficiency Wireless Sensor Networks Clustering Based on SVM
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: A wireless sensor Network (WSN) is organized of multiple nodes in a large area distributed randomly, each node was sending information at same time that led to conflict among them, the goal is to resolve the emerging complex conflict in WSN through the utilization of Procedure for electing the own cluster. This required need to optimize the own cluster election and extending life cycle of network. In this paper a support vector machine (SVM) based on clustering algorithm is proposed during election process. The WSN has remaining energy of node, distance from base station and probability of node serving as own cluster. The own cluster is optimized by SVM algorithm to adaptive inertia weight, it considers nodes within the communication range are regarded as its cluster members such number of own clusters selected to satisfies the optimal number of own clusters, and thereby further improving energy efficiency of the network. The simulation results show that the SVM algorithm is more efficient when compared to other algorithms, also the algorithm proven that period of network stability in balancing consuming energy is more effective and more extending the network life cycle.

articleTitle: Keratoconus Severity Staging Using Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Ensemble Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Accurate keratoconus (KC) staging is vital for improving patient care and guiding clinical decision making. Choosing the right Machine Learning (ML) algorithm is key to effectively tackling this challenge and ensuring optimal performance. This paper presents a detailed comparison of eight ML algorithms commonly used in KC detection, based on a clinical dataset collected by the authors over the past decade. The study investigates each algorithm's effectiveness in distinguishing KC severity stages. Results showed that ensemble learning algorithms outperformed other approaches, with Random Forest (RF) emerging as the top-performing model, achieving the highest validation accuracy of 98.82%. When tested on unseen data, the RF model maintained a comparable accuracy of 98%, demonstrating its robustness, and generalizability in accurately distinguishing between different stages of KC severity.

articleTitle: Clinician-Assisted Exploratory Data Analysis Framework for Early Diagnosis of Keratoconus
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Advances in corneal imaging have generated vast datasets, making it challenging to extract clinically relevant insights. Machine Learning (ML) provides ophthalmologists with essential tools for keratoconus (KC) detection and clinical decision-making. However, effective Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) remains crucial for identifying trends, forming hypotheses, and selecting key parameters to build robust ML models. This paper presents a comprehensive EDA framework that fosters collaboration between AI specialists and clinicians to enable early KC detection. Using statistical and visual techniques alongside expert input, a clinical dataset with 79 features from 2,491 cases is pre-processed, analyzed, and effectively prepared for ML modelling. The analysis identified a key subset of features–just 6.3% of the original dataset–which was used to develop and evaluate the classification performance of several ML models. Among them, the Random Forest model achieved 99.6% accuracy, surpassing previous studies and demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed EDA framework.

articleTitle: Leveraging Generative Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Detection and Classification of Diabetic Retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a severe microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus, causing progressive retinal damage and, if left untreated, leading to permanent blindness. Early detection is critical for effective treatment; however, the current manual diagnostic process performed by ophthalmologists is both time-intensive and reliant on highly trained professionals. This approach faces numerous challenges, including its inefficiency in detecting early-stage DR and the growing global prevalence of the disease. To address these limitations, the adoption of automated, efficient, and accurate detection methods is imperative. Recent advancements in deep learning (DL) algorithms have significantly improved the performance of commercial DR detection systems, enabling more precise diagnoses. This study examines the challenges associated with traditional DR detection and classification, particularly in the early stages, and explores the transformative potential of generative artificial intelligence (GAI). By leveraging technologies like chat generative pre-trained transformers (e.g., ChatGPT), GAI can enhance clinical workflows by generating detailed medical reports, educating patients, and analyzing extensive datasets to uncover actionable insights. This research highlights the integration of GAI as a promising avenue for revolutionizing DR detection and management.

articleTitle: Detection Techniques for Cell-Free Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) systems represent a transformative evolution in wireless communication, characterized by a distributed architecture of numerous low-cost, low-power access points (APs) connected to a centralized network controller. Unlike traditional cellular systems, CF-MMIMO eliminates the concept of cells, with every AP collaboratively serving all users simultaneously. This design eradicates inter-cell interference, significantly enhancing network capacity, reliability, and spectral efficiency. As a corner-stone for future 6G networks, CF-MMIMO aligns seamlessly with the vision of ultra-reliable, low-latency communication, massive connectivity, and ubiquitous coverage. By leveraging distributed APs, CF-MMIMO systems pave the way for energy-efficient, high-capacity networks that cater to the demands of next-generation wireless systems. This paper conducts an in-depth exploration of various detection techniques, including minimum mean square error (MMSE), zero-forcing (ZF), linear precoding MMSE (LP-MMSE), and regularized conjugate beamforming (RCB). Through rigorous simulations and performance analysis, the results demonstrate that while ZF achieves the best bit error rate (BER) performance, RCB emerges as a robust contender, especially under practical conditions with imperfect channel state information. MMSE and LP-MMSE exhibit moderate performance, with LP-MMSE being comparatively less efficient in mitigating interference and noise.

Author Keywords: linear precoding minimum mean square error

articleTitle: Robust Optimization-based Neural Architectures Against Adversarial Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Recent years have seen a rapid development in Machine Learning, which has profoundly influenced many areas of science and engineering. Among them, computer vision takes the leading place, where important tasks are image classifications powered by CNNs. Despite the great performance of CNNs in complicated scenarios, they remain sensitive to so-called adversarial attacks, and deliberate perturbations leading them to incorrect predictions. Besides more innocuous consequences, this has serious security implications for critical applications, in-cluding medical diagnostics, where misclassifications might result in disastrous outcomes. This research work discusses adversarial attacks on CNNs and other DNNs in computer vision, studying a full range of the generation and detection methods with details while discussing intrinsic vulnerability and robustness. It also proposes a learning framework that will enhance the robustness and security of DNNs and CNNs against such adversarial perils. The ultimate goal is directed to an improvement in the reliability of such models in absolutely critical scenarios for safe deployment into applications where accuracy is crucial.

articleTitle: Intelligent Lighting Control: A Neuro-Fuzzy Approach for Optimal Energy Efficiency in Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) specifically designed for an in-telligent control system for domestic lighting in a smart home environment. The aim is to create an efficient model that integrates both fuzzy logic and a neural network to improve the adaptability of the control system. To obtain this type of control, two key inputs are used: the indoor lighting level and the presence of a person. These factors are essential to determine the behaviour of the lighting system in different situations. The ANFIS model is trained using two different learning methods: backpropagation and a hybrid technique. To improve accuracy, eight different membership functions (MFs) are used in three sets of epochs: 20, 50, and 100. The training results give us the best choice of ANFIS model parameters that guarantee the desired performance and minimize errors. The results of the study show that the application of the present approach to lighting systems demonstrates the effectiveness of autonomous control.

articleTitle: Enhanced Load Frequency Control for Standalone Multi-Source Power Systems Using GWO and GA Optimized
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This study focuses on optimizing a PID classical controller for Load Frequency Control in a multi-source power system that integrates gas, thermal, and hydro units. Each component, such as the steam turbine, reheater, and governor in thermal systems, as well as the penstock turbine, drop compensation, and governor in hydro systems, is modeled to represent dynamic responses. Additionally, gas turbine components like the valve positioner, speed governor, and combustion reaction are characterized by specific parameters. Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) are applied to fine-tune the PID gains, aiming to enhance system stability during load fluctuations. It exhibited a settling time of 8.92 seconds, with an overshoot of 0.012 and an undershoot of 0.0268. This marked a significant improvement over the performance of the PID controller, which had a settling time of 46.93 seconds, an overshoot of 0.045, and an undershoot of 0.055. Additionally, the GA demonstrated robust performance, achieving its best result under the IAE cost function with a settling time of 8.63 seconds, an overshoot of 0.000998, and an undershoot of 0.0268-slightly outperforming GWO in terms of settling time under IAE. However, GWO struck the best balance between rapid convergence and minimal overshoot for precision control, making it the most suitable choice for LFC in multi-source power systems.

articleTitle: Unified Framework for a Robust Fdi of a Fluid Benchmark System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a unified diagnostic framework for a three-tank fluid benchmark system based on Hybrid Bond Graph (HBG) modeling, with a focus on enhancing fault detection and isolation (FDI) capabilities under parameter uncertainties. The proposed HBG model captures both continuous and discrete dynamics, accommodating discrete events such as valve switching. While HBG models enable effective diagnosis by generating analytical redundancy relations (ARRs), they are often sensitive to parameter variations, which can reduce reliability in uncertain environments. To address this problem, we introduce an incremental model derived from the HBG that accounts for deviations in system behavior due to parameter uncertainties, resulting in a more adaptive diagnostic process. By incrementally adjusting model parameters within the HBG framework, the proposed approach ensures that generated ARRs remain valid across varying operating conditions and configurations, regardless of minor parameter fluctuations. Simulation results demonstrate that the unified framework significantly improves robustness in fault detection and isolation, even with variable fluid levels, valve states, and component tolerances. This framework offers a practical FDI solution for three-tank benchmark systems with complex configurations, showing strong applicability in industrial settings where parameter uncertainty is prevalent.

articleTitle: Efficient Data Detection Techniques for Massive MIMO Systems Using Improved Newton Iteration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (M-MIMO) technology is a critical driver of fifth-generation (5G) and beyond-5G (B5G) communication systems, significantly enhancing capacity, efficiency, and overall network performance. However, the performance of M-MIMO systems is heavily influenced by the detection techniques employed, which also determine the complexity of the system. To address the trade-off between performance and computational efficiency, this study explores advanced signal detection methods within the M-MIMO framework. This paper introduces two novel hybrid detectors, combining the Gauss-Seidel (GS) and Jacobi (JA) methods with an enhanced Newton iteration (NI) approach, designed to minimize iteration time while maintaining high detection accuracy. By leveraging the upgraded NI approach, these detectors achieve efficient data decoding while significantly reducing computational complexity. Extensive analysis and simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed architectures in terms of computational complexity and bit error rate (BER). In particular, the proposed approach achieves a significant reduction in complexity, lowering it from O(NK<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ NK) to O(NK) for Detector 1, and from O(NK<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ NK) to O(NK + K) for Detector 2, effectively demonstrating substantial improvements in both efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: Project-Based Learning Investigation in Mechatronics Engineering Education at TIU: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Project-Based Learning (PBL) has emerged as a transformative pedagogical approach in engineering education, particularly within Mechatronics Engineering. This study focuses on the impact of using PBL at Tishk International University (TIU) in undergraduate learning experiences and outcomes of projects. The research combined two courses: Microcontroller & Programmer and Special Topics in Mechatronics to investigate how PBL developed technical competence, problem-solving approach, and professional preparation of students. Effectiveness was multidimensionally measured through a structured interview that involved project supervisors and students. The results showed that the students' preparedness for the graduation project had greatly improved, with the supervisors of the projects agreeing that student preparedness had increased by 100%; more than 75% of supervisors made notations on improved problem-solving and technical skills over the non-PBL students. Critical thinking showed a gain at 71.5% in students exposed to PBL, problem-solving at 85.7%, and teamwork at 85.7% over their non-PBL counterparts. Nine practical projects have been completed concurrently, leading to the successful participation of these projects in the National and International Innovation Competitions in Engineering and drawing attention to the potential contribution of PBL in bridging academic learning with the challenges faced in industry. This, despite several challenges, including resource allocation and project timeline management, this research offers ideas that would be very helpful in having PBL integrated more effectively in curricula in engineering, which will make students ready for a challenging and multidisciplinary environment.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Lung Tumor Detection Approach Using YOLOv11 and Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Computer-aided diagnostic systems have proven efficient in accurately and effectively diagnosing lung cancer. How- ever, the speed of diagnosis remains a prime challenge for spe- cialists who need immediate results. This study proposes a novel approach for rapidly detecting lung cancer through CT scan images. The proposed approach relies on YOLOv11 for region-of- interest detection integrated with Vision Transformer for feature extraction and classification. Three distinct datasets were used for training, validation, and testing. Thus, an unseen dataset was used to further assess the model's performance. Moreover, Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) was used to enhance the model's trustworthiness and comprehensibility. The proposed method achieved high performance, completing training and validation in about half a minute, with an accuracy of 92% and a precision of 96%. When tested on the DLCT dataset, it achieved a performance of 97.86%. The proposed model achieved very promising results with real-time diagnosis speed.

articleTitle: Robotic Teleoperation Control Using PSO-Tuned Fractional Order Active Disturbance Rejection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Bilateral teleoperation systems have become essential for enabling precise remote manipulation in fields such as robotic surgery and hazardous material handling. However, these systems face significant challenges, including time delays, environmental uncertainties, and nonlinear dynamics, which can affect their stability and performance. This research aims to investigate the application of Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) to address these challenges. ADRC is chosen for its real-time estimation and compensation for disturbances, even with limited knowledge of the system model. Additionally, the study incorporates enhancements such as Fractional-Order control and optimization techniques, including Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), for parameter tuning. A simulation study is conducted to assess the performance of the proposed controller in tracking control of bilateral teleoperation systems with 3-DOF and 4-DOF manipulators. Results illustrate the superiority of the fractional order ADRC in disturbance rejection and trajectory tracking compared to linear ADRC, making it a promising solution for teleoperation applications.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Optimizers for Breast Cancer Segmentation in Ultrasound Images Using U-Net
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study on the impact of various optimizers Adam, SGD, AdaGrad, and RMSprop on U-Net-based segmentation of breast cancer in ultrasound images. Using a synthetic dataset of breast ultrasound (BUS) images, generated via Data Expansion Network (DEN) and Probability Map Generator (PMG), the performance of each optimizer on segmentation metrics such as Dice coefficient, IoU, and accuracy are evaluated. Results demonstrate that the Adam optimizer yields the highest segmentation accuracy, while other optimizers exhibit specific strengths that may benefit different aspects of training stability and convergence.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuned Yolo V-10X: Real-Time Object Detection for Autonomous Vehicles Under Multiple Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Detecting objects such as vehicles, buildings, pedestrians, and road signs is indispensable to advancing the concept of autonomous and self-driving cars. Furthermore, an autonomous vehicle (AV) must accurately detect its surrounding environment to operate reliably. Most object detection (OD) techniques perform adequately under typical weather conditions, including cloudy or sunny days. However, their efficiency decreases significantly when exposed to Adverse Weather Conditions (AWCs), including days with sandstorm, rain, fog or snow. Complex and computationally costly models are required to achieve high accuracy rates. In this study, we present an improved OD system in AWCs for autonomous vehicles (AVs) using the single-stage deep learning (DL) algorithm YOLO (You Only Look Once) version 10. To evaluate our system, Vehicle Detection in Adverse Weather Nature (DAWN) dataset is used. It comprises real-world images captured under various types of AWCs. The experimental findings confirm that the suggested method is effective and surpasses state-of-the-art OD approaches under AWCs.

articleTitle: Depression Detection Using a Hybrid CNN-BiGRU-BiLSTM Model With BERT Embedding and Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: Depression is a mood disorder that causes a persistent feeling of sadness and loss of interest. Also called major depressive disorder or clinical depression, it affects how you feel, think, and behave and can lead to a variety of emotional and physical problems. Automatic detection, as in a clinical interview can be derived from various modalities which includes video, audio, and text. Among them, detection from text data has emerged as a crucial task in mental health monitoring. In this study, we propose a hybrid deep learning model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) layers to enhance depression detection accuracy. Using BERT embedding for robust feature extraction, the proposed model processes social media or clinical text data to identify signs of depression. Additionally, we incorporate a novel data augmentation technique using synonym replacement to address data imbalance and improve generalization. Evaluations are conducted using key performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. With an accuracy of 86.2 %, the results demonstrate that the combined CNN-BiGRU-BiLSTM architecture, alongside BERT embedding and augmented data, significantly improves classification performance compared to traditional models. This approach shows promise in contributing to more effective automatic depression detection systems.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Enhanced Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Mobile Robot Trajectory Tracking
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 22nd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: In recent years, the application of robotics has significantly advanced many fields, providing robust performance and efficiency in complex tasks without the need for human intervention. Robot control is a key area of robotics that has received a lot of interest and technological development. Active Disturbance Rejection Controllers (ADRCs) are widely adopted due to several features, including their ability to maintain robust performance and effectively reject disturbances. The manual tuning of controller parameters is time-consuming and highlights the need for automation.
